headline: A safety catch I designed would have jammed the moment it was needed most. The engine lane spotted it before it shipped, and it is fixed.
matters: Reference bytes for the game were twice frozen without this repo's real test suite ever running, and a wrong number rode along unnoticed. I am building the enforcement so that cannot happen quietly again. My first design had a trap: if a freeze failed its tests for a reason that needed a second freeze to fix, the first one could never be signed off - and the only ways out were to hand-edit the record or to sign off something that had not passed. Those are precisely the two things the catch exists to prevent, so it would have taught people to do the wrong thing at the exact moment it mattered. The fix lets a failed freeze be formally set aside instead, but only by actually doing the replacement, so it cannot become a shortcut. Separately, the engine lane answered the question I could not: the signature has to record how many of the strict checks actually ran, because that is the one number a suite run WITHOUT the strict flag cannot produce - and a suite without the flag is otherwise fully green and indistinguishable.
detail: REFREEZE-NEEDS-STRICT, branch feat/refreeze-attest, not yet landed. Original sketch: per-entry attestation on provenance.toml Entry, two-valued (attested/absent), enforcement on entry N+1 while N unattested, self-disarming ratchet mirroring aeon_rev, boundary derived from the chain never pinned to an entry number. Aeon (aeon-f2) refuted the two-valued shape: a freeze whose strict run legitimately fails is permanently unattestable, so a byte-moving fix requiring freeze N+1 deadlocks the chain with hand-editing or a false attestation as the only exits. Adopted their three-valued state: attested / absent / superseded-abandoned, where abandoned REQUIRES naming the successor entry so it is only reachable by performing the next freeze. Ruled here under this lane's standing autonomy on assembler internals rather than escalated to the hub. Also adopted their attestation contents: (1) sigil SHA + aeon_rev, (2) golden CRC32s read from the blobs at run time not copied from the entry, (3) count/names of strict-gated bodies that executed - the only value a non-strict run structurally cannot produce, since strict_gate() early-returns those bodies and a non-strict suite is fully green. Parts 1-2 stop reuse, part 3 stops vacuity. Per-field audit question given to the agent: 'could this value be right if the run never happened?' Ship condition: poison with SIGIL_STRICT_GATE unset must refuse the attestation or record zero strict bodies. Aeon released the hub's HOLD-THEN-LAND on their own account (they run strict before pushing, so chain 172 is attestable), so it lands after their 172 pushes rather than in the morning. Precedent chains: 169 c8e87ecb, 170 174f4300; stale constant SFX_BODY_LEN 2046 vs region 0x8DA=2266.

headline: Four numbers describing the cartridge's own size had quietly gone wrong, and the one that fooled the search was the one that looked most correct.
matters: These are the figures that say how long each build of the game is. Nothing in the project read them any more, so nothing could notice when they drifted - one was right the day it was typed and wrong within a month, and it stayed wrong for 28 days. The search that found them was looking for numbers typed in by hand, so it missed a fourth that was written as a NAME instead of a number: it looked like the computer had worked it out, and it hadn't - it was the wrong build's figure. The fix removes the stored numbers entirely, so the game works them out fresh every time and there is nothing left to go stale. There is now a check that would have caught all four.
detail: OFFCANON-ROT, merged at 959958c7 (via 731af546). Four off-canonical assembled_len values in native.rs: demo 0x11224 vs 0x1121c (+0x8), config_b 0x434d0 vs 0x8b6f0, config_a 0x5f65a vs 0xa7e70, and lean_profile spelled `pins::ASSEMBLED_LEN` (the canonical shape's bar, +0x1082 past lean's own). The fourth was invisible to a sweep enumerating large hex literals - 'a wrong value spelled as a symbol looks derived'. config_b's 0x434d0 was correct when typed 2026-07-30 (94768171). Stored field deleted; assembled_len() derives per call and panics rather than substituting. New gate crates/sigil-harness/tests/offcanon_assembled_bar.rs, 4 tests, source-only so it never skips; agent corrected its own overstatement - cross-tool for the canonical pair, temporal for the off-canonical five. REGION_A_LMA deleted: dead AND wrong (0x3DE vs derived 0x3D6). Suite 3947/0/4 = 3951 declared, zero skip:, zero ratchet:, clippy clean, AEON_DIR=.sigil-ref-353aaa49@353aaa49, log .sigil-verify-landing-b.log.

headline: We now know how much of the game's code the timing model can actually speak about - and measuring it turned up two ways the model can hand back a confident wrong number.
matters: The emulator lane was waiting on this figure. The answer depends entirely on how you count, so it is reported two ways rather than one, and the gap between them is itself the finding. More useful than the headline number: of the game's routines, about one in six could carry a timing budget and exactly one does. The two defects are the kind worth having found early - the timing built-in never checks which of the console's two processors it is on, so on the main chip it can hand back a figure measured in the other chip's clock units; and the sound-side adder tops out instead of refusing, returning its ceiling as though it were an answer. Neither can be reached by today's code, both by luck rather than design. Nothing is fixed yet; they are written down with the conditions that would close them.
detail: CYCLE-FRACTION, merged at 959958c7 (via 88a95ad9). Note docs/superpowers/notes/2026-08-27-cycle-fraction.md; tool crates/sigil-harness/src/bin/cycle_fraction.rs, in no suite. Measured over all seven shipped_shapes at aeon 353aaa49. By instruction site: 68000 66.88% exact / 33.07% ceiling / 0.04% unmodeled; Z80 72.89% / 0 / 27.11%; combined 68.08/26.48/5.43. By proc worst-bucket: combined 12.22/64.53/23.25 - the ~7x divergence reconciles to 98% of the 68000 ceiling bucket being the linker-relaxation ruling, not data dependence (only 0.65% of 68000 instructions vary with operand values). Layer B: 63/357 (17.6%) 68000 procs and 10/142 (7.0%) Z80 procs could carry @budget; 1 does. Four brief corrections upheld: model is four-valued not three (Branch pairs); 'cannot time' is two different things (five unreachable trap #0 vs a deliberate Z80 demand subset); shipped_shapes() misses the seam-1 resident sound blob entirely (registry walk sees zero Z80 in every sound-on shape); Layer A/B is the axis, not the denominator. Defects ledgered: eval_cycles has no CPU dispatch (builtins.rs contains zero 'cpu' refs; verified firsthand) - a 68000 nop returns Z80 T-states, all 24 call sites are (cpu: z80) today; z80_cycles::span_cost accumulates u16 saturating_add, returns 65535 where it owes a refusal, ~20x headroom. Queued as CYCLES-CPU-GUARD and SPAN-COST-WIDTH. Clippy type_complexity fixed at desk in 959958c7 (aliases only).

headline: The check that was supposed to catch tests quietly opting out could never have failed - it was reading output the test runner throws away.
matters: Before a batch of the game's reference bytes is accepted, this repo runs its tests and requires that none of them quietly opted out. That requirement has been part of the ritual for a long time and it has never once been able to fail: the test runner hides the output of any test that passes, so the warning line it was looking for was always discarded before anyone could grep for it. Every landing that reported 'none opted out' - including two of mine tonight - was reporting on an empty page. It took one word on the command line to fix. The automated nightly check already had that word and was never blind, so the damage is bounded to hand-run landings. Separately, 30 tests across 11 files worded their opt-out in ways the check could not match even with the output visible; those now share one spelling, defined in one place, with a lint that fails if a new one drifts.
detail: Verified firsthand before acting: same binary, `cargo test --release -p sigil-cli --test seam2_dac_emit` gives 0 skip-shaped lines, `-- --nocapture` gives 2. libtest captures passing tests' stdout/stderr. OVERSEER.md bar at :320 now carries `-- --nocapture` INSIDE the command span (bar 25 corrective 2). scripts/nightly_source_gates.sh:262 already passed it - so the earlier claim that the automated backstop 'shares the ritual's blind spot' is true for the SPELLING and false for CAPTURE; corrected in the doc. SKIP-TEXT-HOLE landed at c1718cb2 (via df21c18f): brief said 27 sites/9 files, measured 30 code paths/11 files - +2 in seam2_colink_probe.rs spelling `skip ` with a space, +1 in resumable.rs with no skip vocabulary at all and NOT strict-gated. The reported 176 `skip:` was a raw literal grep incl. doc comments; actual announcement sites 136 -> 166. SKIP_MARKER now defined once in test_support.rs and EXTRACTED by sed in the nightly script (exit 2 if unextractable). New gate skip_marker_lint, 2 tests, 6 poisons each red-then-restored, in SOURCE_GATES (40). Suite 3950/0/4 = 3954 declared, cross-checked by `cargo test --workspace -- --list` = 3954 (different enumeration parameter). clippy exit 0, audit unclassified=0, marker hits 0 with capture OFF.

headline: A landing gate I wrote would have taken the nightly safety net dark on its first night, by tripping the exact alarm it was built to restore.
matters: The new lint prints a one-line summary saying all the opt-out warnings are correctly worded - and that summary quoted the warning text itself. The nightly check greps the log for that text and shuts the whole lane down when it finds it, on the assumption that a test went quiet. So a perfectly healthy run of the new gate would have looked exactly like the failure it exists to detect, every night, starting the first. It only surfaced because I had just fixed the blindness above; with the old command the line was invisible and it would have shipped. The gate now describes the warning instead of printing it, and refuses to run if its own summary ever contains it again.
detail: Caught at landing on branch fix/skip-text-hole. The census used `{SKIP_MARKER:?}` which renders `"skip: "`; nightly_source_gates.sh does `grep -qF "$SKIP_MARKER" "$OUT"` -> note COULD NOT RUN, exit 2, whole lane dark. Confirmed by running the nightly's own extraction+grep against the green log: 1 match, the census line. Fixed at 0ce85540: census says 'the canonical marker', plus `assert!(!census.contains(SKIP_MARKER))` with a diagnostic naming the rendered line. Proven red-first by restoring the interpolation - fails at skip_marker_lint.rs:308 quoting the exact string - then restored and re-verified green. Note the shape: this is the parcel's own subject (a check that reports nothing reads as a check that found nothing) turned back on the parcel, and the ONLY reason it was visible is the --nocapture fix landed minutes earlier.

headline: Nine hand-typed cartridge addresses in the test suite were all wrong, and one of the tests they sat in was proving nothing whatsoever.
matters: These tests deliberately damage the game's data and check the bytes come out different. Nine of them had the address typed in by hand, and all thirteen numbers were out of date. Eight still did their job by luck. The ninth did not: it was looking in the release build for data that only exists in the debug build, so the bytes it wanted were not there whether or not the test damaged anything - it would have passed no matter what broke. It now reads the debug build and has a second arm that fails if the undamaged version stops matching. The proof this was fixed the right way rather than merely re-typed: three of the nine addresses moved again during the session, and the suite passed across that with no edits at all.
detail: STALE-PROBE-BASES landed at c1718cb2 (via 1087a139/6f1aa514/2ea69be5). Nine sites, thirteen literals, across tranche{2,4,5,6}_negative_probes.rs; all thirteen differed from their pins; all ruled INPUT (lma_base fed to place_sections), none an oracle - contrast native_full_rom.rs:180 where repin generates the pin from the listing convsym resolves, genuinely circular. My 'not load-bearing' characterisation REFUTED for the ninth: doctored_af_delete_produces_different_bytes sliced s4.bin but PARTICLE_ANIMS is DEBUG-only (plain_len==0); the bytes 00 02 04 02 02 02 FB 00 occur nowhere in s4.bin's 718,999 bytes and exactly once in s4.debug.bin. Vacuous, not merely stale. Also found: the region `size` beside each base is hand-typed too, 7 of 8 disagreed (ledgered, no gate). New gate probe_base_hygiene.rs keyed on region NAME so no allowlist, 60 blocks covered; 5 poisons, one came back GREEN revealing a real per-line marker hole that blanket-cleared every region on a line - hardened, now red at vectors_port.rs:327. Regions that moved mid-session: particle_anims 0x2ac78->0x2aca8, sonic_anims 0x29ff0->0x2a020, act_descriptor 0x16764->0x16794.

headline: Reference bytes for the game can no longer be accepted on top of a batch whose tests were never actually run - the tool now runs them itself.
matters: Twice recently a batch of reference bytes was frozen without this repo's real tests ever running, because the written recipe was missing one setting that turns the strict checks on. Nobody audits a command line for a missing setting, so the recipe looked complete and was inert. The fix stops relying on anyone remembering it: the tool runs the suite itself, sets that switch itself, and records what it found. The record contains one number that a run WITHOUT the switch physically cannot produce, so a signed-off batch cannot be a batch that was never properly tested. If a batch genuinely fails its tests and the fix needs a fresh batch, the old one can be formally set aside - but only by someone who actually ran the tests and got a red result, so setting-aside cannot become the easy way out.
detail: REFREEZE-NEEDS-STRICT merged 729cd642, docs 9040dc36. `refreeze --attest` spawns the suite with SIGIL_STRICT_GATE=1 set on the child (unconditional, refreeze.rs:526), adds --nocapture, stamps its log before cargo writes. Witness: test_support::strict_gate() records file:line ONLY on the branch that already observed the flag set, so strict_bodies is structurally 0 when unset; measured 29, matching an independent static count of 29 `if !strict_gate(){skip;return}` sites (two enumeration parameters). Refuses on: dirty sigil tree (verified end-to-end by me, not taken from the report), AEON_DIR unset/dirty/!= tip aeon_rev, zero suites, zero passed, zero bodies, missing --expect-test, HEAD moved mid-run. Witness file is per-run-stamped AND explicitly removed pre-run, so a stale witness cannot be inherited. Three-valued entry state (attested/absent/superseded) after aeon refuted my two-valued sketch as deadlocking a legitimately-red freeze; abandonment requires a NAMED successor AND a recorded red run, closing serial supersession. Schema is pure-append ([entry.strict] at EOF attaches to the last [[entry]]): 22 lines added, 0 deletions, all 171 predecessors byte-identical; nothing backfilled. Aeon's `_port` log-harvest witness REFUTED by measurement: 43 of 46 hits are cargo's pre-binary `Running tests/...` lines, flag-off reproduces the count. Agent claimed 53 new tests; measured delta is 40 (+40 #[test], -0), tree totals 3994 by both git grep and `cargo --list`. Suite 3990/0/4 = 3994 declared, exit 0, marker hits 0 with capture off, ONE expected ratchet: line (the new attestation ratchet, disarms at first --attest; NOT the aeon_rev pairing ratchet). clippy -D warnings had 3 errors on this branch - never run by the agent, my brief did not demand it back - fixed at desk in 729cd642.

headline: A test that quietly passed whenever the compiler could not read its own input now fails loudly - and a second test's description was wrong about both its numbers and its reason.
matters: The first test damages a piece of code on purpose and checks the damage is caught. If the compiler failed to read the test's own input, the test passed anyway - so it could not tell 'the bug was caught' from 'we could not read the file'. The thing it tolerated failing is this compiler's own parser, in this same repo, so there is no situation where that is expected; it now fails loudly, in every mode, matching what the other fourteen tests in that file already did. The second is a description at the top of a test claiming a piece of the game's data is the same size in both builds. It is not, and the stated reason was wrong too - it said the code contains nothing debug-only, while the file's own body already knew it does. Rewritten to describe where the real numbers live instead of copying them, so it cannot rot again. Nine more test descriptions with the same defect are written down for later.
detail: Landed ea43b0d3 (752a305f, 8b400f65). RESUMABLE-STRICT: my ruling was always-fail; agent confirmed with a better argument than mine - strict_gate()'s own doc comment defines the legitimate absent population as an EXTERNAL tree (aeon is a sibling working copy, not vendorable), and the context/with grammar is sigil_frontend_emp compiled into the same test binary, so no checkout/CI shape/feature flag can make it absent; strict-only would also blind the ordinary dev loop, which is where a parser regression is introduced. Local idiom clinches it: the file's own lower() helper already asserts perrs.is_empty() unconditionally and 14 sibling tests route through it. Red-first BOTH directions: old code + sabotaged grammar = GREEN exit 0 (proving vacuity), new code + same sabotage = FAILED exit 101 with no SIGIL_STRICT_GATE set. skip: marker removed with the eprintln/return; lint census 166 -> 165, the departing site from the seen-by-both bucket, i.e. the population definition applying rather than a site being hidden. Agent also found the header's CAUSAL claim false - it said parallax has no __DEBUG__ code, while engine/level/parallax.emp:594 carries `if DEBUG == 1` with a raise_error guarding the sec_effects contract, verified by me in the reference tree; the file's own body comment already knew. New header names the pin and the mechanism, no digits. Ledger: 10 files by a stated mechanical criterion (## Shape headers, hex literals vs the named pins::Region), disagreeing with a handover's unnamed 'fifteen'; recorded as a FLOOR with its criterion rather than reconciled, kill condition is a doc-comment lint. Suite on merged tree 3990/0/4 = 3994 declared, exit 0, skip: 0, ratchet: 1 (expected), clippy real exit 0, both enumerations 3994. Master gained only .md between the run and the push (verified: no .rs/scripts/toml), so no re-run.

headline: Both ways the timing checker could hand back a confident wrong number are closed - one of them so that the mistake can no longer be written down at all.
matters: The game has two processors. The tool that measures how long a stretch of code takes only knows how to time the sound chip, but never checked which processor it was on - so on the main chip it could return a figure measured in the wrong chip's clock, and one padding instruction is spelled the same on both, so the wrong number would have looked right. It now refuses, and the refusal explains which chip you are on, why the number would be wrong, and the two correct ways to ask. I had suggested it fall back to the main chip's own timing table; the agent showed that would be worse - that table often gives an upper bound rather than an exact figure, and this tool's answers get compared for equality, so it would assert a cost the machine need not pay. The second: the sound-side adder used to stop at its ceiling and return the ceiling as an answer. It now cannot overflow at all - the limit is derived and checked when the compiler builds, so narrowing it is a build failure rather than a silent return of a wrong number. I reproduced that proof myself.
detail: Landed fc3dee76 (2a72ba48, bad9390a, cb29b2a3). CYCLES-CPU-GUARD: ruled REFUSE not dispatch; require_z80_for_timing raises [cycles.wrong-cpu] on Cpu::M68000 and on absent ev.cpu. Agent's deciding reason overturned my brief: ~1/3 of the shipped 68000 stream prices Fixed{exact:false} (a ceiling, mostly because operand width is a linker-relaxation fact the evaluator precedes), and cycles() is compared with ==, so summing ceilings into an equality asserts a cost the machine need not have - i.e. defect 2's shape in a new place. Also pad_to_cycles cannot dispatch (its pad units are Z80 nop/jr; jr has no 68000 spelling) and units differ (3.58MHz T-states vs 7.67MHz). Old [cycles.unknown-op] 'add it to z80_cycles' text now reachable only from a Z80 proc where it is correct. SPAN-COST-WIDTH: TStates=u128, MAX_SPAN_T_STATES derived in-type from Cost::Fixed's u16 payload x (isize::MAX/size_of::<CodeItem>()), plus const _: () = assert!(<= i128::MAX) proving the lossless reach to Value::Int; const overflow is a BUILD error so the width is compiler-checked, not runtime-watched. Reproduced by me: narrowing to u64 gives error[E0080] 'attempt to compute 64051194700380387_u64 * 65535_u64, which would overflow', restore exit 0. The ledger's own suggested u32/u64+bail fallback misses the derived bound by ~230x. 8 gates, all red-first; ONE poison came back green and it was the matcher not the guard (asserted the refusal doesn't name z80_cycles, but the new refusal legitimately names it as the table it reads) - retightened to the real property, re-proved red. Brief corrections: two pad_to_cycles sites not one; the dense case does emit but is rejected downstream by the 68000 mnemonic table (diagnostic-quality, not miscompilation) while cycles() and SPARSE pad_to_cycles built completely clean with no diagnostic - worse than the case I flagged. Sharpening: assume_some (one of the two shared spellings) appears 4x in shipped 68000 code, so the collision is live in the corpus though not inside any cycles() span - exposure still zero. cycle-fraction note NOT invalidated (it reads instr_cost only); re-run reproduces every figure byte-for-byte. Suite 3998/0/4 = 4002, three-way enumeration agreement (git grep 4002, --list 4002, declared 4002), clippy exit 0, skip: 0, ratchet: 1 expected.

headline: The example behind one of tonight's findings turned out to be innocent, and admitting it caught a real flaw in the fix I was building.
matters: A test lane's shrinking count was blamed on a check going missing. It was a retired feature, counted correctly. Correcting it exposed that my own fix assumed a number that nobody had ever checked was stable - so it is being measured instead of assumed.

headline: The assembler has been telling every other tool that its own source might not match, permanently, because of a file no build reads.
matters: Two other lanes were about to write that warning down beside their measurements and read it as proof they were safe. A warning that never switches off cannot tell anyone anything. The cause is removed; the warning itself keeps showing the old value until the assembler is next rebuilt, which is deliberately being held until the engine lane's freeze finishes.
detail: sigil e5bd4a4f: docs/lane-status.json added to .gitignore. sigil --version reported 'tree: dirty at capture - 0 modified, 1 untracked' on every build; the untracked file was the lane status file, present by design, read by no build, so the -dirty suffix (also in the compact version string consumers quote) was a constant. aurora enumerated across all six lanes: four track it, aurora ignores it, sigil alone was untracked-and-not-ignored. Chose ignore per contract/LANE_STATUS.md rule 5 - local disk authoritative, tracking turns a per-dispatch file into commit noise, and a tracked copy would be MODIFIED on every status write, strictly worse for the dirt signal. tree: is a build-time snapshot so the reported value is now stale rather than stuck; the tell that the fix reached the banner is a revision that is not fbf60abd. Not relinking while aeon's seven-ROM freeze pins target/release/sigil.

headline: The check that guards our reference bytes could be switched off one piece at a time without anyone noticing. It now names the piece that went missing.
matters: It only refused when every one of its 29 checks had been skipped. Deleting one left 28, which it accepted as a pass - so a check going dark looked exactly like success. It now works out what should have run by reading the source at the time it runs, so retiring a check honestly needs no edit to a stored list, and quietly deleting one is refused by name.

headline: The engine lane's red test was mine to fix, and the reason it broke will break again for the same reason.
matters: Their new record of which object drew each sprite lives in one file and is read from another. My test for that code compiles it on its own against a hand-written list of the addresses it is allowed to reach out to, and the new name was not on the list. The fix is one row. The finding is that the list has two halves: every address in it is worked out from the source automatically, and none is ever typed by hand - but WHICH names are on it is maintained by hand, so anything they add breaks exactly one of my tests at a moment I do not control. This is the second time; the first is still sitting in the file with a comment admitting it. I deliberately did not put a number on how widespread it is: three ways of counting disagreed with each other, and two of them were not even subsets, so any single figure would have been an undercount presented as a measurement. The engine lane then improved the fix I proposed - checking the two lists against each other in both directions, rather than just building one from the other, because a difference can be proved and a reading cannot.

Sprite_Owner declared engine/ram.emp:1145 inside `if DEBUG == 1 @shape_divergent`, read via `lea Sprite_Owner, a6` (abs.w, so the VMA is in the region bytes) at sprites.emp:235; aeon parcel cbd04ba8, their tip 7511a440 by ls-remote. My own lane-log at 06:36 today already recorded that capture, not silence, is the mechanism and that the nightly passes --nocapture - I contradicted my own banked finding from memory. Withdrawn, and the escalation it was supporting withdrawn with it.

headline: The crash-screen guard could report success by having nothing to check. It now proves, per build shape, that it had something.
matters: When the game crashes, a debug build prints a report naming where it happened. That report only works if a particular block of vendored code is the very last thing in the cartridge, and a check guards it. The check had a hole: if the block went missing entirely - renamed, or dropped by a re-layout - it returned success, because it looked for the block, did not find it, and treated that as nothing to complain about. A missing subject and a satisfied rule produced the same answer. It now works out, for each of the seven ways we build the cartridge, whether that build is supposed to carry the block at all, and complains in both directions: a build that should have it and does not, and a build that should not and does. Six of the seven carry it. The check also refuses if either group is empty, because a rule that applies to nothing passes trivially.
detail: ISLAND-PIECE-2. Merged 9d9e164d (branch fix/island-non-vacuous-arm). check_error_handler_is_last takes expect_island; authority is native::declares_error_handler_island, reconciling profile.debug||crash_report against registry membership of engine.debug.error_handler and refusing when the two records disagree or the exclusive island/release_fault split is lost - upstream of every label the build emits, so not the listing asserting agreement with itself. Merged-tree verification on a reference built at the chain-173 aeon_rev 33d905b8, four ROMs CRC32+size matched to the tip entry: 4023 passed / 0 failed / 4 ignored across 349 result lines, --list 4027, 4023+4=4027 exact; 0 skip: lines with capture PROVABLY off (the --nocapture rerun is 174 lines longer, extra lines being passing tests' stdout); both island binaries present by name with their test names; clippy -D warnings exit 0; audit gates=41 unclassified=0. Log stamped pwd/HEAD/branch/AEON_DIR at .tgt-a6a7c23d-evidence/suite-9d9e164d.log. DEVIATION RATIFIED (bar 7): the dispatch brief nominated games/sonic4/map.toml's order list as the per-shape authority; it is a union across targets carrying both ReleaseFault and BusError (:143), verified firsthand at aeon origin/master, so a complying agent would have shipped a green meaningless gate. PROCESS DEFECT, mine: I pushed this merge while telling the aeon lane it was held - `git push origin master` is scoped to a ref while I was holding a commit; the verification became post-hoc confirmation rather than a gate. Banked with the pgrep-scope instance as one shape.

headline: Numbers written in comments cannot be wrong, because nothing runs them. Fifty-nine of ours were, and five were teaching people not to look.
matters: A comment saying a piece of the game is a certain size is read by people and executed by nothing, so it can be wrong for months without anything going red. Five of ours went further: they claimed a region was the SAME size in both the normal and the debug build, when the generated table says the two differ. A wrong number misinforms you; a wrong claim that two things match tells you there is nothing to check. Several files disagreed with themselves inside one screen. The fix is not to write in the right number - that is the same mistake with a fresher date - but to point at where the number actually lives, so it cannot drift again.
detail: PROSE-SWEEP, merged in 537869e6 (branch sweep/prose-bounds, commits 49666597 + b60e79cb + notes 248b18f5/3d8c9d64). 8 false-or-stale '$X both shapes' length claims; 51 stale reference windows across 15 port gates, of which ZERO matched a current pins.rs region. Two enumeration parameters run and reconciled (numeric-literal-in-comment A1-A4: 1348/1432/4661/1309; bound-language keyword K1-K5: 276/107/30/14), queries listed verbatim and re-runnable in docs/superpowers/notes/2026-08-27-prose-bounds-sweep.md, because an empty sweep and a grep that never matched its subject are the same artifact. Joint commitment with the aeon lane, each lane over its own tree. Patterns that transfer: the half-fix (a pointer added, the copy left beside it) is the dominant mode; the invariance claim rots before the number does; derived diagnostics that interpolate {max} are immune to the class. Explicitly NOT covered: decimal-only bounds (A3's 4661 hits untriaged), .emp/.asm, and empyrean's SIGIL_* specs - a real gap, unswept by either lane. repin.toml BLOCKED (other lane's file) and its per-region comments carry the identical stale claims, so the generator's INPUT is stale too.

headline: Our freeze tool wrote a record file it could not read back, noticed, and left it there. It corrupted one tonight.
matters: Every time the two projects are frozen together, a line is added to a record file saying which build is which. That line includes a sentence a human wrote. If the sentence contained a quotation mark - and sentences quote things - the tool wrote a file that was no longer readable, checked it, found it broken, and left the broken file in place. Nothing about it looks broken: it looks authoritative, and every later check fails with a line number instead of a cause. It is now checked before it is written, quotes are handled properly rather than refused, and the file is replaced in a way that cannot leave it half-written.
detail: FREEZE-WRITES-HOME ledger half. Merged in 537869e6 (branch fix/provenance-ledger-integrity, f386109c). Root cause: render_entry hand-built TOML basic strings while toml_str - the correct escaper - sat directly beneath it, serving the other two renderers; its doc comment asserted its fields 'never carried a quote', and that sentence WAS the defect (the same prose class as the sweep above, in the function it broke). Now: every field through toml_str; fault_in_prose refuses only what a one-line field cannot show verbatim (control chars incl. raw newline) naming character and byte offset; fault_in_key guards the table-header interpolation which has no escaping fallback; append_block parses in memory BEFORE installing; write_atomic temp+sync_all+rename, both bare fs::write sites gone (grep on the committed blob returns 0). Gate is the CLASS not the instance - 'after any refreeze that reports an error, provenance.toml still parses' - proven red-first reproducing tonight's exact 'expected newline, #' at line 16 col 9, plus the_refusal_accepts_every_entry_the_chain_already_holds as a control so an over-strict refusal could not land quietly. RECORDED: temp-and-rename would NOT have prevented this - an atomic rename installs a complete-but-invalid file atomically - and that conflation was the fix both lanes had agreed on this morning. TAGGED, still open: no end-to-end refreeze --freeze has run through the assembled CLI path.

headline: The assembler can now say whether the edits in its tree actually reach the program, instead of warning about every stray note.
matters: The assembler prints whether its own source tree has uncommitted changes. It could not tell an edit to real code from a note left in a documentation folder, so it warned constantly and was therefore read by nobody. It now works out which files the program is genuinely built from and reports against those. The engine lane reads this line, and their reader used to treat any word it did not recognise as safe - so a new word would have silently switched their check off. They fixed that first; ours landed second.
detail: VERSION-DIRT-CLASSIFY. Merged in 537869e6 (branch feat/version-drift-classify, 8c1dce0f + 9d71d8f4, held ~5h at the aeon lane's request and landed only after their guard fix aeon 4b43bdda and their attest at sigil 866ab37a). build.rs derives the compiled-source closure from cargo metadata --no-deps (transitive non-dev path-dep walk, every closure manifest a rerun trigger, no hand-written crate list); banner gains closure:, closure-revision:, closure-paths:; tree: reports clean-sources when uncommitted changes fall outside the closure. Four gates, each proven red by mutation: reported paths equal cargo's answer re-derived at test time; reported revision is the last commit touching those paths (proven under a docs-only tip, the only tree state where they differ); no compiled source reaches a file the closure calls unreachable via #[path]/include*!; the banner discloses which way it errs. False-clean gated in both places. NOTE, measured 2026-08-27 and it kills a hoped-for remedy: narrowing the paired-landing banner to the closure does NOT silence it - pins.rs is a non-dev path dep of sigil-cli, pub mod pins carries no cfg(test), and native.rs (the module the CLI calls at build time) reads pins values - so that banner is a TRUE positive every time it fires.

headline: The freeze tool now writes into the copy of the repo you run it from, not the one it was built from - and it says out loud when those differ.
matters: Freezing the two projects together is done from a private working copy so the shared one is left alone. That protection did not work: the tool wrote into whichever copy it had been BUILT from, so a freeze meant to stay private silently modified ten files in a colleague's working copy. It now writes where it is run, refuses by name if it cannot tell where that is, and prints on every run which copy it was built from versus which it is operating on - because the underlying trap is that a pre-built program carries its old paths, options and defaults silently, and a stale one answers confidently about all of them.
detail: FREEZE-WRITES-HOME, both halves, merged 38fa6096 (branches fix/harness-root-derived 5335f01e + fix/repin-root-passed 0aada5a2). Half one: HARNESS_ROOT demoted to a display-only BUILT_FROM; root derived via git rev-parse --show-toplevel of the cwd + crates/sigil-harness, verified against BOTH markers (golden/provenance.toml and repin.toml), refusing by name with resolved/from-where/expected-and-missing; SIGIL_HARNESS_ROOT override verified identically, set-but-empty refused; NO fallback to the constant, held by a source lint that was mutation-checked. Half two was NOT optional: refreeze shells repin via cargo run, and cargo REUSES an artifact across trees sharing one CARGO_TARGET_DIR - measured here on the real crate, build-from-B finished in 0.01s still baking tree A's path - so half one alone would have written goldens to one tree and pins.rs to another, a split freeze from a tool reporting success. repin now takes --harness-root and refreeze passes it on both spawn paths incl. REPIN_BIN; disagreeing flag-vs-env is refused naming BOTH rather than ranked. Six red-first reversals, each restored; headline gate spawns the real binary with the real argument list from a third valid tree and asserts non-vacuity first. announce_root prints unasked on every invocation and states the verdict in words when the paths differ - specified that way at the aeon lane's insistence, against their own convenience, because a diagnostic behind a flag only reaches people who already suspect the binary.

headline: Two of my test expectations broke on the engine lane's parcel; one is now written so it can only fail for its own reasons.
matters: Their change to how slopes are judged shifted things by two bytes, and two of my checks went red. Neither was their fault. One was a test compiling a single file with a narrower notion of where the project starts than the real build uses, so a file path that works in the real build missed in the test. The other is a deliberate tripwire holding a hand-typed address, designed to force a human to notice and explain movement. Rather than typing in the new number I anchored it to a generated one plus an offset, so a shift somewhere else in the program can no longer set it off, while a change in the part it actually watches still does.
detail: SLOPE-HARNESS-FIX, f7266c65. Cause 2: test_p2_player_states_port lowered with include_root narrowed to games/sonic4/player and embed_base None, so the parcel's new root-relative embed("engine/data/sine.bin") joined onto the module dir; both fields moved to the aeon root, matching main.rs and soundbankhead_port.rs. Cause 1: Ground_Move_Cap derived from the build (plain 0x10914, debug 0x10A24) not transcribed, then written as pins::P_STATE_GROUND.plain/.debug + 0x2F4 - the intra-region offset grew 0x2F2 to 0x2F4 in BOTH shapes, which says the +2 landed INSIDE the region ahead of the symbol rather than sliding the region whole, a sharper statement than the +2-both-shapes I was given. PROCESS DEFECT, mine: I first named test_p1_player_port to the aeon lane, having grepped for the SHAPE of the cause and stopped at the first match instead of tracing from the failing-test names I already held; caught only because their uncommitted red-attest record listed the six by name. The artifact kept for honesty was load-bearing for correctness inside the hour. I also described the fix as one line when it needs both fields, the exact separation they had corrected me on an hour earlier.

headline: The file-embedding word in our language works from the project root - except for one file, which is exempted by name in a line of my tool.
matters: When engine source embeds a data file, the path is read from the project root. One file writes its path relative to itself instead, and it works only because a single line names that file specifically. So a new file copying that style silently fails, and the style it copies is not a feature - it is an exception. I could not answer this by reading for most of the day; it took a trace plus deliberately breaking the exception to prove the line was doing the work rather than just sitting there.
detail: EMBED-BASE-RULE, note landed 6943cde3. Mechanism is native.rs::build_emp's embed_base_for closure: `if id == "engine.math" { math_dir } else { aeon_root }` - a third closure I had missed after finding two module-independent ones. Proven by trace to resolve_sandbox_path with observed values at the containment check, corroborated by the traced build being byte-identical to the frozen s4.bin (34c67ea6/718999) so it IS the ROM path, and by counterfactual: gating the arm off reproduces the two predicted [sandbox.path-escape] errors. Two prior hypotheses refuted first (a try-root-then-fallback resolver; math.emp being dead code). Further: only `data` items thread embed_base - const/equ/offsets/table/dispatch take include_root alone; and the base is the CONSUMING evaluation's, not the defining module's, so one spelling is legal in one item and refused from another. Proposal to the owner (language surface, so his call): respell math.emp's two sites root-relative and delete the exception, byte-neutral, making the rule uniform and stateable. Caveats kept from the agent: only canonical plain was actually built, and the rule is asserted for embed() not import().

headline: Checked which layout rules the build already enforces before asking anyone to enforce them again - three did, and one nobody had written down does not.
matters: We were about to hand the engine lane eight layout rules to police. Three of them the build already refuses to proceed on, so handing those over would have built a second guard for a rule that already stops the build - work for nothing, and a second place to keep in step. Two are genuinely unguarded, and one of those is new: a deliberately empty gap in the cartridge has nothing checking that it stays empty. That was proven by filling it and watching the build accept it, then proving the same check DOES fire on a different violation - so the pass is the check declining to look, not a broken test.
detail: EIGHT-CONSTRAINTS-RECHECK, merged 61826768 (branch audit/constraint-recheck, 136332d4). already-asserted+demonstrated: R1a (validate_placement [map.undeclared-island]/[map.anchor-absent]), R3 (relax::bank_diag), R8 (check_error_handler_is_last - all three of the inventory's outstanding asks landed in-tree since at 1a03c75c/83b6610e/2247b0f2). NOT asserted: R1b, R1c, R1d, R6 (negative; only a warning in a binary no ROM build runs), R9 (negative, NEW, no inventory row). R9 demonstrated absent with a positive control on the same loop. R3's coverage is narrower than the inventory records: bank_diag skips any section without a bank: declaration (verified firsthand) and .emp makes bank:/vma: mutually exclusive, so soundbankhead is vma:-phased and outside it and dac_banks has no section declaration - both bank heads the anchors name are unchecked and rest on R1c, which nothing asserts. Two inventory premises rotted: map bases are no longer cosmetic, and seam2::bank_anchors_from_str now keys anchors BY NAME on the shipped path, giving up the invariant the ledger comment rests on. Seven predicates delivered in aeon's five-field shape, value as derivation not number. R2/R4 unclassifiable and said so. NOT a closed set: aeon's build-side gates unenumerated, check_object_bank_budget unclassified, off-canonical shapes not individually checked. Also flagged to aeon, not touched: dac_banks.emp's header still says $48000/$50000, superseded by the re-layout to 0x90000/0x98000.

headline: Wrote the check for the reserved gap, and it immediately found that the gap's own declaration has been wrong by six bytes since August.
matters: The cartridge reserves an empty span for a small piece of sound code, and the engine's settings file declares where that span ends. Nothing had ever checked the declaration against reality. The new check found that real content sits six bytes inside the declared gap - and my own existing test already pinned the true addresses, so the cartridge has been right and the declaration wrong the whole time. I did NOT switch the check on: three of the seven ways we build would go red, and the fault is the declaration, not the layout. Bending a new check to accommodate a wrong declaration would defeat the reason for writing it.
detail: HOLE-INTERIOR-UNGUARDED, merged 6775b449 (branch fix/hole-interior-reserved, a0d8dcd9). native::hole_interior_faults: hole opens at `after`, runs to `at`, filled_by's module is the permitted occupant DERIVED from the shape's registry; every other byte-emitting overlap is [map.hole-interior-occupied] naming hole, intruder, head label and occupied sub-span. Five distinct refusals for the unmeasurable arms (anchor-unresolved/ambiguous, bounds-degenerate, filler-unknown/absent) so the vacuous case announces itself - rebuilding the declining-to-look defect one layer up was the live risk. Both maps declare at=0x3FE; boot_data_port pins rom[0x3d0]==0xAF, idle nonzero 0x3d0..0x3f8, rom[0x3f8]==0x9F, so the idle is 0x3D0..0x3F8 and boot_tail's PSG byte sits 6 bytes inside the declared interior; the comment's $3d8 start is wrong too. Declared at aeon a7375682 2026-08-01, untouched while boot grew +8 and the idle body went 38->40. Positive control: correcting only `at` returns clean for all three affected shapes. Sound-on shapes report says-nothing not pass (when=sound_off). NOT wired into validate_placement - deliberately. Suite 4068/0/4 vs 4058/0/4, failing sets empty both, +10 exactly the new tests; all seven shipped shapes byte-identical. [map.hole-anchor-missing] pinned - it had no test anywhere and had never been observed to fire.

headline: An error the compiler threw away could put a WRONG BYTE in the cartridge while reporting nothing wrong at all.
matters: When the compiler works out a constant's value ahead of time, it did a quick trial evaluation first - and if that trial failed, it threw the error away and treated the failure as if the constant simply had no fixed value. Those are not the same thing. The consequence turned out to be worse than a missing number: the constant silently took a DIFFERENT file's value instead of its own, so a build could emit 400 where 4 was correct and report no errors. Not a value that looks obviously wrong - a value that looks plausible. The trial failure now reaches the person building, while the ordinary case of a constant that genuinely has no fixed value stays quiet.
detail: CONST-EMBED-SWALLOWED, merged 659371e3 (branch fix/const-fold-diagnostics, 85950508). fold_const_literal returned Option<i64> and dropped its diagnostics; None already meant ordinary-non-literal, so a FAILED eval was indistinguishable from one with nothing to fold. Root mechanism, found by the agent and not previously known: the probe calls eval_const_with_root WITHOUT embed_base, so it resolves embed() against include_root while real lowering resolves against the module's asset dir - probe raises [embed.not-found], error discarded, no fold, and the CONSUMER's SCALE answers instead of the definer's. Gate vs unmodified master: errors=[], image=[1,144], 400 where 4 is right. Now a three-way ConstFold; the quiet arm is corpus-derived (probe instrumented over all seven shipped shapes: 182 Error occurrences, 36 distinct, 100% unknown-name/unknown-function, zero other classes) and fails loud - rewording either message surfaces them. Faults drain through the existing seen_across_modules filter so a re-raised fault reports once. One caller, fully enumerated (ConstFoldCache::folded -> collect_pub_comptime -> ambient_items/ambient_from_uses, 4 driver sites). Byte-neutral: an errored eval still never folds; seven shapes CRC-identical AND golden/anchor gates green both sides, so matched to frozen provenance not merely to each other. Suite 4074/0/4 vs 4068/0/4, failing sets empty, +6 exactly, zero skip lines. NOT fixed and booked: the embed_base skew itself (fixing changes what folds = moves bytes). Enumeration with positive control found two other discard sites left unfixed: eval/guards.rs interp_one_part/interp_one (message degraded, error still raised) and emp_census.rs (tooling, but it is read as the authoritative clobber-undeclared list, so a truncated parse understates it).

headline: A failure whose fix changed no bytes could never be marked superseded - so a finished, tested check sat unusable behind it.
matters: Every paired freeze appends a line to a record file, and a failed run stays recorded as failed until a later freeze replaces it. But a freeze only appends when the output actually changes - so when a failure's cause turned out to be in the test harness rather than the game, fixing it produced identical output, appended nothing, and the failure stayed the newest entry indefinitely. That went from cosmetic to blocking today: a new safety check was finished and tested and could not be switched on until the record moved. An explicit request to supersede now appends even when nothing moved; without that request, nothing changes.
detail: FIXPOINT-CANNOT-SUPERSEDE, merged ce0b610b (branch feat/supersede-passes-fixpoint, 61251ef6), pushed 8dc62906. The bail was `if equals_tip { FIXPOINT; return }` with supersede consulted nowhere; now `byte_neutral && supersede.is_none()`, falling through to the UNCHANGED append gate (green tip, unattested-on-armed-chain and unarmed chain all still refused). provenance.rs +249/-0, purely additive: plan_freeze as a pure decision, freeze_into owning the ledger half. One ordinary [[entry]], no schema; legibility from the entry's own note. All seven provenance:: consumers outside refreeze verified to read tip_target only, so duplicate goldens are invisible to them. Anti-evasion intact: abandoning the new tip still costs a real red attest. Six red-first mutations, each failure shown and restored, including the two refusal sub-cases proven separately. Suite 4074/0/4 vs 4068/0/4, failing sets empty, +6 exactly. REVERSAL, logged as such: refused this morning on 'one instance is not enough to redesign a ledger on', which was right on that evidence; changed on n=2 plus a blocked consumer. NOT red-first: the early-refusal improvement at the pre-rebuild gate, gated by reasoning only - flagged rather than absorbed.

headline: The engine lane's freeze finished, my hold came off, and the ledger it wrote is one step short of finished in a way that would have stopped their next one.
matters: Their record of the run says the check came back failing. It does not say that - it says nothing at all, because the run never got written down. That is a much easier fix (just run it again, and it should pass now), but it also means the very next change that moves bytes would have been refused at the gate with no obvious reason why. Told them before they hit it.
detail: Hold lifted at sigil f6f67d2f; all three binaries measured at raise-time md5 (sigil 85ba502f, refreeze 8cf597eb, repin 37657e41), corroborated by aeon quoting the same SIGIL_BUILD pin. Chain 176 debug-rings-gate, aeon_rev 55e0858f, sigil c84a98c2 on origin/master. Entry 176 has NO [entry.strict] block; the 'repair not a re-run' refusal at refreeze.rs:551 is gated on tip.strict.is_some(), so --attest is available. append_gate returns Refused (not NeedsSupersede) for an unattested tip, which is what would have blocked the next byte-mover. Also refuted aeon's proposed finding that --supersede-tip assumes a byte-moving fix: ce0b610b (on origin/master since 2026-08-27 12:30) makes an explicit --supersede-tip pass the fixpoint for exactly the byte-neutral case; and entry 175 is already properly superseded by 176, so there is no red tail. Hub had banked a note on the wrong premise; asked aeon to retract it. Freeze reconciles: s4 0261de2b/719029, s4.debug fee02557/735500 (+46 off 735454, the corrected delta), lean 3a307f1f/674830 same length different bytes, config_a 735868, config_b 610421, both demo shapes unchanged.

headline: A fixture the engine lane renamed broke three of my checks, and the obvious repair would have quietly broken them worse.
matters: Their rename was correct and my check was correct; the gap was that nothing reads these references unless a build runs, and builds only run when a change moves bytes. So it surfaced two parcels later inside someone else's work, looking like their fault. The tempting fix - point at the renamed file - would have aimed three checks at a completely different rule while their names and comments still described the old one. Picked a different fixture on three stated grounds and added a check that costs no build, so the next one gets named the morning after instead.
detail: sigil 06e1e376, pushed. extra_entry.rs POISON_TWO_RESTORES -> poison_band_nested.emp, fragment 'two bands are live on CRAM entry'. Rejected poison_four_bands (P2a DELETED the one-band rule the old fragment pinned - a rename that is also a re-aim); rejected poison_band_orphan_restore/span_mismatch/h2_sh (COUNT 2, would redden the two [Error]==1 assertions); rejected poison_band_no_owner ('carries no band id' appears in 3 poisons + the guard, so the matcher cannot witness which rule fired). Corrected aeon's premise that the candidates were untouched since P1: c4bd725a edited all three, though for nested only comments. New test every_aeon_fixture_this_file_names_still_resolves: build-free exists sweep, asserts poison_band_nested present AND poison/gone.emp absent (if gone.emp is ever created, a_missing_extra_entry_errors_loudly silently stops testing its subject while passing). Both spellings now constants so sweep and cases cannot drift. Red-first x3, each restored: renamed path, created gone.emp, one-char fragment perturbation. Verified in isolated worktree + own CARGO_TARGET_DIR against detached aeon b42141bc (entry 177 aeon_rev); 8/8 SIGIL_STRICT_GATE=1. Main checkout untouched, target/release/sigil still 85ba502f, no relink announcement owed. Class fix noted for the nightly source-gate lane. Also: I was reading a ledger one chain stale for the whole exchange because aeon had three commits local - undetectable from my side.

headline: The engine lane was one minute from rebuilding our shared tool out of a stale copy of my tree, and the result would have looked perfectly healthy.
matters: They told me they were about to rebuild the shared assembler and quoted the version they expected it to pick up. They had the right version in mind but were pointing at the wrong thing: the rebuild compiles whatever is sitting in my working folder, and mine was two commits behind - two commits that were their own freshly-finished work. Had they started, the tool would have been stamped with the older version while every check agreed with itself, because the check that looks closest at this compares the tool against the folder it was built from, and both would have been equally stale. I pulled the two commits first, so it built the right thing. Out of that came a rule I have now written down: when the shared tools are rebuilt, the announcement lists a fingerprint for EVERY tool the build produces, generated by a command rather than typed. My own file had a hand-written list of three, and the one it left out was the only one that actually feeds their cartridge build.
detail: Relink of target/release/sigil requested by aeon at ~02:40Z. Their message cited my origin/master b73bf420 as the reference; my main checkout was at 4eca7d93, 2 behind (b23cba42 refreeze chain 178 + b73bf420 attest, both landed through their lane). `git merge --ff-only b73bf420`, pure ff, empty b73bf420..4eca7d93, verified against `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/master` not the tracking ref. Relink completed 02:49Z: sigil md5 85ba502f->495986ee, baked rev 914846bf->b73bf420, confirmed here firsthand. RULING (mine, sigil-internal gate design, d-2 'just do it' territory): announcement emits md5 for every executable cargo build --release produces, via `find target/release -maxdepth 1 -type f -executable -printf '%p\n' | sort | xargs md5sum` - command verified to run as written, 12 lines today. Rejected aeon's proposal to name two binaries: the existing hand-list named sigil/refreeze/repin and omitted emit_sound_blob, which writes z80_sound_blob.bin, declares its output byte-deterministic from sources AND toolchain version in its own header, and is invoked by aeon build.sh as an ARTIFACT step that dies without it. n=2: aeon build.sh's ASSEMBLER PROVENANCE banner already recorded sigil sitting three days behind unnoticed. Landed in docs/OVERSEER.md under GUARD THE ARTIFACT.

headline: Their freeze was sound but its written description of what moved was wrong, and that description is what the next session will read.
matters: They asked me to check their arithmetic rather than take it, which was the right instinct. The record says the addresses shifted uniformly with one oddity; measuring all 134 of them says there are three distinct groups and two oddities, not one. The part worth their attention is that the shielding fix's 16 bytes show up in the release build's address field and never in the debug build's - which may be entirely intended, but nobody had noticed it either way. Nothing about the cartridge or the tests is wrong; only the sentence describing it, which is already committed and pushed, and which is exactly the kind of claim nothing in a repository ever checks.
detail: Chain 179 (13a6d3c8 refreeze tilt-and-instashield, 520d07f6 attest, aeon 4ba7cb92). Their commit message: 'Pins move +0x80 plain / +0x70 debug ... PLAYER_SNAP_TO_SURFACE moves +0x72 in both shapes'. Measured over all 134 changed entries (45 Region + 89 Pin) by two methods sharing no code - diff parse, and differencing named symbols read from pins.rs at both revisions. Actual: three tiers. +0x70 BOTH shapes on 21 entries (13 P_STATE_* pins, 6 PLAYER_* regions, 2 u32) plus PLAYER_COMMON whose base is unmoved while its length grows +0x70 both shapes (the tilt). +0x72 both shapes on TWO entries - PLAYER_SET_STATE as well as PLAYER_SNAP_TO_SURFACE. +0x80 plain / +0x70 debug on the remaining 112. Max debug delta anywhere in the field is 0x72; max plain is 0x80, so the insta-shield's 0x10 never enters the debug pin field though s4.debug still grew +156 total like plain. Mechanism deliberately NOT asserted to them - flagged as their measurement. Also: their message said shield=14 B, their commit says 16 B; 0x10 says the commit. Suggested repair is a correcting note in the next chain entry, not a history rewrite.

headline: The open question in my last note is answered, and the answer is that my instrument could not see what I asked it about.
matters: I reported that the shielding fix's bytes appeared in the release build's address list and never the debug one, and asked whether that was intended. They measured it three ways and the bytes are in the debug build - a tool that decodes the debug cartridge's own contents runs the new code nearly seven thousand times. What I was reading is a list of landmark addresses, and there is enough spare room between that code and the next landmark in the debug build to swallow the growth before it reaches one. So the list showed nothing while the cartridge had changed. I had scoped the claim to the list and asked rather than asserted, which is the only reason it cost a measurement instead of a wrong entry in the record. Both of us also learned why we disagreed at all: this freeze bundled two separate changes, so measuring start against end could never say which one moved what. Neither of us thought to look at a point in the middle until they did.
detail: Refutation accepted. aeon's three witnesses: symbol Ability_InstaShield$from_jump present in BOTH listings at +$10 from routine head (plain $11614->$11624, debug $1172C->$1173C); tools/instashield_gate.py decoding s4.debug.bin, 6912 executions, PSTATE_JUMP + PSTATE_ROLLJUMP fired, OK; debug neighbours InstaShield_Spawn $1175C->$1176A and InstaShield_Main $117A0->$117AE, +14 both. Mechanism: local growth absorbed by slack before CharacterDefs in debug; plain has less slack and alignment rounds 14 up to 0x10. Their three-revision table's ENDPOINTS verified here against my own committed pins.rs - CHARACTER_DEFS plain 0x11EA0->0x11F20 (+0x80), debug 0x11FC0->0x12030 (+0x70) at 13a6d3c8^ and 13a6d3c8; middle column (e1f412ed, tilt-landed shield-not) is theirs. 14 vs 16 settled: 16 = gate block = plain tier-3 delta; 14 = routine net growth 48->62, the fix letting d1 carry the state byte into the roll-jump cancel. Both correct, neither said which. My (1) two straddlers and (2) three-tier field stand, taken without qualification. Two bars banked in docs/OVERSEER.md: count byte-movers inside an A/B range before differencing its ends, and a pin field measures where pins are not where code is (bar 16(d) on a positive quantitative instrument).

headline: The prediction we wrote down in advance came true, and their run found two real defects in my own tooling.
matters: Before they measured, both lanes committed in writing that their change would alter values without shifting anything, so no addresses should move - and that if one moved we would stop and talk rather than quietly re-record it. It held, and I checked that myself from the committed change rather than taking their word. Recording it as a promise kept rather than just a green run, because a prediction that comes true is only worth something if it is on record that it was made first. Two defects in my tools fell out of them using them: the tool that rewrites our reference cartridges cannot be aimed at a chosen copy of the tree by a flag while its safer sibling can - point it wrong and it quietly works on the wrong tree instead of failing - and it runs longer than an agent can hold a command open, so being killed leaves half-rewritten reference files behind. Both are now on the list. They also found a better way to prove one of these builds actually ran, using a file of mine neither of us had thought to read that way.
detail: Chain 180 BALL-SEATING landed: sigil fa0e6540 (freeze) + 6b3ef068 (attest), aeon 03ed1f1c. Falsifier DISCHARGED, verified here not taken: pins.rs untouched in fa0e6540 by git show --stat on that path; ROM sizes unchanged 719205/735818; repin --check reported pins.rs unchanged. Attest 4081/0/4, 352 suites, 29 strict bodies, ratchet held, 0 skips, 4085/4085. BETTER WITNESS: golden/offcanonical_sizes/s4.txt moved exactly 2 lines on this freeze, both CRC headers (golden_crc32, assembled_anchor), with assembled_end=0xa5c90 and every label held - verified on fa0e6540. That is POSITIVE where 'pins.rs unchanged' is an absence consistent with a build that never ran; banked as preferred for length-neutral parcels. DEFECTS: refreeze has 0 occurrences of harness-root vs repin's 2 (verified), so aiming it needs SIGIL_HARNESS_ROOT + SIGIL_BUILD or it operates on its compile-time tree; and refreeze outlives the 10-min foreground cap (timeout does not help, harness clamps), aeon's first attempt killed holding 5 half-written goldens. Queued as REFREEZE-NO-HARNESS-ROOT and REFREEZE-PARTIAL-WRITE. Hold cleared in OVERSEER.md; chain 181 re-arms it on a fresh grant and is currently stopped on the owner (cost larger than the d-40 card described).

headline: I quietly worked around a wrong reference instead of saying it was wrong, and the other lane had to raise it against themselves for anyone to learn.
matters: They pointed me at one marker for a landing that actually has two - one holding the evidence, one holding the sign-off. I went to the right one because that is where the data was, verified it, and never mentioned that the marker I had been given was the other one. My checking was right and the silence was the defect: a correction nobody states teaches nobody, the wrong habit survives, and the next reader without the instinct to go looking finds an apparently empty landing. They caught it against their own message. I have written down both the correct form for citing these pairs and the fact that routing around a bad reference silently is itself the failure. Separately, I had banked a new proof-of-build slightly stronger than it earns; they stated its two limits while it was fresh and I have added them, because the version I wrote could be read as sufficient on its own.
detail: aeon cited 'sigil 6b3ef068 (freeze ball-seating chain 180 + attest)' - one SHA for two claims. Verified here: fa0e6540 carries the goldens (11 files incl. s4.bin/s4.debug.bin, provenance +54); 6b3ef068 touches provenance.toml only (+21, the attest block). Both reachable at origin/master. Correct form banked: 'freeze fa0e6540 · attested 6b3ef068'. I had verified at fa0e6540 without flagging that the handed SHA was the attest. WITNESS LIMITS added to the offcanonical_sizes paragraph, aeon's statement: it witnesses that a build ran and produced these labels, is SILENT on which source it used (composes with the assembler md5, does not replace it), and is positive ONLY for length-neutral parcels - on chain 181 (debug +4, 282 symbols +16) the table moving is expected and it reverts to something to reconcile.

headline: A reported flaw in our freeze tool turned out not to be real, and the fix that was queued for it would have broken tonight's freeze.
matters: The engine lane hit two problems while freezing last night and reported both. One is real and is being fixed. The other described our freeze tool as able to quietly work on the wrong copy of the project with nothing going wrong on screen. I checked it by running the tool from two different directories rather than by re-reading the report: it uses whichever copy you are standing in, and it prints a loud warning when the program was built somewhere other than where it is working. The queued fix was to make it refuse unless told explicitly which copy to use - and the normal, correct way to run it is exactly the way that would then have started refusing, at three in the morning, with nobody awake to unblock it.
detail: Retracts OVERSEER.md defect 1 of the chain-180 pair. refreeze main() calls resolve_harness_root(&cwd, ROOT_OVERRIDE) at src/bin/refreeze.rs:1037 -> git rev-parse --show-toplevel; module doc states it outright. Behavioural proof, prebuilt target/release/refreeze md5 05a1f3c0501c94638d53bfa5620503b5, --check (read-only) from two cwds: shared checkout -> operates on sigil/crates/sigil-harness, tip ball-seating chain 180; .worktrees/lane-c -> operates on lane-c's tree, tip migmask chain 51, with THIS BINARY WAS BUILT FROM A DIFFERENT TREE printed. --harness-root is the parent->child protocol (refreeze derives the root, passes it to repin via ROOT_FLAG). Survives narrower: SIGIL_BUILD does default to <root>/target/release/sigil, but capture_goldens.sh:52 tests -x and exits by name, so friction not silence; the aeon-side tree is separately hard-enforced by resolve_aeon_rev (set, git repo, HEAD resolves, clean). Class: peer-measurement-vs-mechanism; their grep counts reproduced exactly, the causal story did not.

headline: My status card was invisible to you for six minutes because I used the word 'done' in it.
matters: The file that tells your console what this lane is doing has a fixed list of words for an item's state, and 'done' is deliberately not one of them - a finished item is supposed to leave the list entirely. I wrote it anyway when retiring an item, and one wrong word makes the console reject the whole file, so everything true in it went dark with it. Nothing on my side reports that; the hub found it by polling. Fixed, and I checked the rest of the file against the contract while I was there and found a second breach it had not reached yet. Worth knowing because another lane did the identical thing three days ago, which is what got 'done' banned in the first place - it is the word anyone naturally reaches for, so the rule runs against the grain and will keep being broken.
detail: Dominion: 'queue[4] has state "done"; expected doing | next | open | blocked' (contract/LANE_STATUS.md at empyrean origin/main). Row REFREEZE-NO-HARNESS-ROOT, the retracted refreeze finding; removed from queue rather than restated, its landing already in lane-log and its reasoning in OVERSEER.md. Second breach found unprompted: three items marked next, contract requires exactly one; now one next, two doing with agents live. Invalid window 08:03:22Z-08:09:19Z. Contract line notes done was ruled out 2026-08-26 after aurora's file was rejected whole for the same value - n=2, different lanes. Suggested to the hub (their call, not a request): fail-soft on this enum by dropping the row, since that is what the contract already prescribes for a finished item; likely evidence for their existing FMT-LINT item rather than a new one.

headline: Fixed the instruction defect that caused my own two agents to trip over each other tonight.
matters: Every brief I write tells an agent which copy of the engine tree to use, and there was already a rule saying that must never be left optional. Both of tonight's briefs followed it and the agents still collided, because the rule only covered SETTING the value - not that each agent needs its OWN copy, nor that a freshly made copy contains no built ROMs at all and so is a build job rather than a reference. One agent's rebuild kept deleting the files the other was reading. The instruction now states all three things, and says the quiet part: a fresh copy is not usable as a reference until someone builds it. Also recorded that this kind of interference can just as easily make a result look GOOD as make it fail, so 'it passed when I ran it again' settles nothing.
detail: Closes BRIEF-DEFAULT-POINTS-AT-HIM. OVERSEER.md AEON_DIR section widened from unconditional to unconditional+exclusive+prepared. Evidence: 213 reference-missing failures on first contact with a fresh detached worktree (engine/debug/generated absent, demo debug unresolvable); one 'SIGIL_STRICT_GATE set but reference missing: .aeon-hole-wire/demo.bin' in an otherwise clean 4090-test run, green on isolated re-run. Framing: a path is not a state - the brief named a value to set where it needed a property to hold. Sigil 75b8f8ed, verified at remote.

headline: Both of tonight's fixes are landed: a reserved-space check that now actually runs, and a freeze that can no longer leave half-written files.
matters: The first closes a gap where the compiler declared a region of the ROM reserved and then never checked anything stayed out of it - it was written weeks ago and held back because the engine lane's map had a stale number that would have turned three builds red for a fault this lane could not fix. They corrected it, so it is switched on and refuses in both directions. The second means a freeze killed part-way through can no longer leave damaged reference files behind, which cost the engine lane a run last night. Both were held unmerged all night so they could not move the ground under the engine lane's own landing, and merged only once that was pushed.
detail: master ec0a0f98, verified at remote. Merges 1710581d (parcel/hole-interior-wire) and 765c31fc (parcel/refreeze-atomic-capture) onto aeon's chain-181 attest 46a0d06b. Full strict suite on the merged tree: 4099 passed / 0 failed / 4 ignored, 354 suites, 0 skip lines, exit 0, SIGIL_STRICT_GATE=1, AEON_DIR at a prepared worktree of 544e6e57 (the new provenance aeon_rev, all four shapes built). Reconciles exactly: 4081 baseline + 9 + 9. Signature tests confirmed present by name, not inferred from the total: every_live_hole_holds_only_its_filler, some_shipped_shape_declares_a_live_hole, a_kill_during_staging_leaves_the_complete_old_committed_set, the_direct_write_path_leaves_a_truncated_golden_when_killed_mid_file. Byte-neutrality re-proven against the NEW tip: the merged tree rebuilt s4 06d2ccf6/719205, s4.debug a9676c6b/735818, demo 3415e3ef, demo.debug 7599953e - aeon's chain-181 values reproduced independently.

headline: The freeze record can now tell you when it points at a revision that no longer exists - and it found one.
matters: Every freeze pins itself to a revision of each repo, so a record cannot quietly belong to a different version of the code than it claims. Nothing ever checked those revisions still EXIST - only that they were the right length, so a revision that had been rewritten away passed forever and silently. Chain 181's record points at exactly such a ghost, created when the engine lane rewrote history between measuring and publishing. The check now reads the real remote, names the entry and the revision, and tells apart three situations that look identical but need opposite responses: you forgot to fetch, you have not pushed yet, and the revision is gone for good. The last one is the only real fault, and it is the one nothing could see.
detail: master 71de2646, verified at remote. Merges parcel/ledger-rev-reachability (71de2646) onto f237dd73. Full strict suite on merged tree: 4116 passed / 0 failed / 4 ignored, 355 suites, 0 skip lines, exit 0, SIGIL_STRICT_GATE=1, AEON_DIR at prepared worktree of 544e6e57, clean tree. Bar 4099 -> 4116, +17 in the one new binary tests/rev_reachability.rs, +1 suite; reconciled and confirmed by name in the log. Live walk: 181 entries, 33 revisions, all 24 aeon reachable vs their origin/master 734ab392, 8/9 sigil reachable, 1 DIVERGENT = entry 181 strict.sigil_rev bfbedc11. AEON_DIR unset gives 24 COULD NOT MEASURE and exit 2 rather than reading clean. FOUR states, not the three I briefed: the agent showed 'present but unreachable from remote' also covers a correctly-rebased commit awaiting its push; discriminator is reverse ancestry. It also refuted my leaned-toward ratchet design: during the ritual the next entry's own commit is legitimately unpushed, so 'not pushed yet' and 'orphaned' are the same measurement at write time and a hard rule would redden the gate it must not break. Structural prevention written up for aeon: push the freeze commit before attesting; currently a warning, refusal is their ruling.

headline: A freeze that gets interrupted can no longer look finished - the fix is in.
matters: Freezing the reference copies of the game runs four steps. Only the first was safe. Stopped in between, it left brand-new copies sitting beside an out-of-date size table, out-of-date addresses and an out-of-date record - each of which reads perfectly well on its own, so nothing looked wrong. The engine lane hit the worst version of this tonight: a stopped freeze deleted one of the game files outright while the usual check still reported everything clean, because those files are deliberately excluded from version tracking. Now the run keeps a note of where it got to, and the next one refuses to continue over a leftover and tells you exactly which files are fresh and which are stale.
detail: parcel/freeze-step-gap merged ec870c3e, pushed; 4139 passed / 0 failed / 4 ignored over 358 test binaries on the merged tree; the 20 new gates named in the log; strict path proved live by a reference-less positive control (vblank_port fails by name) rather than by the flag's presence in the command. Reference: exclusive copy of .aeon-land-182 at aeon e99a2ca7, 1203 tracked paths hash-verified, 4 ROM CRCs matching ledger entry 183.

headline: This landed on a decision made in your place while you slept, and it can be undone cheaply.
matters: You told the coordinating session it could decide for you overnight. It decided this lane should stop waiting and land the finished fix, because the engine lane was about to freeze and waiting would have cost a whole cycle with the hazard still open. I checked that you had actually said it - found your words recorded, dated and published - rather than taking the claim, and I have written down that I never heard you say it myself. If you would rather this had waited, it is one revert.
detail: Hub ruling under the widened overnight grant, empyrean 3de429d on origin/main; scope line 'rules in his place wherever a lane is blocked on a decision'. Landing recorded in docs/OVERSEER.md.

headline: The compiler now states where each piece of the game must sit, instead of working it out from where it happens to sit.
matters: Until now, how strictly a chunk of the game had to be positioned was never written down anywhere - it was worked backwards from a frozen table of addresses. So re-freezing that table could silently change a requirement with no positioning code changing, which has already happened once and quietly broke hand-built padding elsewhere. Writing the requirements down revealed three that the old scheme could not even express: two sound sections that must start on a 32 KB boundary and the object code that needs a 64 KB one. All three were being held true only by hand-placed anchors, with the actual requirement recorded nowhere. This is the first of the rules that has to exist before those frozen tables can stop being the authority, which is what ends the freeze-per-byte ritual you asked about.
detail: parcel/declare-section-alignment merged 15cf396c, pushed. 4153 passed / 0 failed / 4 ignored over 359 binaries on the merged tree against a freshly built aeon def98ee5 reference whose four ROM CRCs match ledger entry 186. Reconciles against master's 4139/0/4 over 358: +14 new tests, +1 binary. Byte-neutral: whole-ROM and off-canonical byte gates pass. Two validators, both always-on in build_rom_chained_with_listing; three red-first demonstrations against the real corpus.

headline: Every pinned region now says where it ends - and finding out how many did not revealed 58 nobody had ever counted.
matters: Large parts of the ROM were pinned with a start but no stated end, so each one silently ran up to wherever its neighbour happened to begin, absorbing any gap. That is stable only while a frozen table holds the neighbour still, which is exactly what we are retiring. The number I briefed was 79, taken from a warning the previous pass had used as its progress meter. That warning compares addresses, and when a neighbour's label sits flush against a region's last byte an address cannot tell that apart from a label the region owns - so the meter would have read zero with 58 more cases of the same fault live underneath it. The real population is 140. Thirty-four were converted outright with nothing changing; the rest now declare what kind of contract they have, and an undeclared one refuses instead of passing quietly.
detail: parcel/explicit-region-ends merged 0df56c8c. 4156 passed / 0 failed / 4 ignored over 360 binaries on the merged tree (log stamped pwd+HEAD, cargo_exit=0), against the aeon def98ee5 reference matching ledger entry 186. pins.rs: 34 doc-comment lines, zero constants; repin --check says unchanged; all seven shipped shapes' golden gates green. Red-first is permanent: the gate strips each of ~50 declarations from the live manifest in turn and asserts refusal.

headline: The dead placement path is out of the assembler, and the list I had written for removing it would have deleted a live safety check.
matters: The list was right when I wrote it. Nothing runs a list, so nothing could tell it when one of its targets grew a new user - the only reason the check survived is that I told the agent to prove the path dead from the code instead of trusting my own note.
