headline: The divergence I sent an agent to fix turned out not to exist - and the probes it wrote to prove that found a real one underneath, where a macro argument could come out as a copy of the argument before it.
matters: I had this backwards and it is worth saying so plainly. The parcel that landed this morning recorded that the real assembler upper-cases macro arguments while we keep them as written, which would have meant the two of us disagreeing about which symbol a name refers to. It does not: that upper-casing is the assembler's case-insensitive mode, and the Sonic 2 disassembly assembles with that mode switched OFF - its own build script passes the flag and says so in a comment. The original observation came from probing without it. What the same probes did find is a genuine silent-wrong-answer we shipped: we substituted a macro's arguments by replacing one name at a time across the whole line, so a value pasted in for the first parameter was still sitting there when we went looking for the second one, and it got pasted again. A macro called with two arguments could emit the first one twice and say nothing. That is fixed, and the fix is one pass over the line. The real assembler cannot make this mistake because it resolves parameter references when it captures the body, so pasted text is inert - which is the kind of design reason worth knowing rather than just matching.
detail: Landed at master 85a026a7 (merge of parcel/shift-allargs-case, three commits: 620f8b7d the fix, 05ecd2e2 the note, 5e8cf46a a doc-comment whitespace pass), pushed and verified by ls-remote. THE REFUTATION: asl's upper-casing is its global identifier fold, applied to every argument value at BIND time (visible at entry as [AA][BB] before any shift), not at the post-shift ALLARGS rebuild; entry ALLARGS is the invocation's own text, which is the only place the unfolded spelling shows through and is what made the rebuild look like the transform's origin. s2disasm/build_tools/lua/common.lua:773 runs asl with -U ('forces case-sensitivity', its own comment at :769) and sigil's three asl vector generators pass it too; listings self-report *CASESENSITIVE : 1. Verified here firsthand at that line, not taken. Both contexts closed with -U listing rows: a composed name Mix_{"Ss"} resolves to 0077 in both, and the folded spelling errors in both (asl #1010 / sigil unresolved symbol Mix_SS), so neither can silently pick the other symbol; text-into-data emits byte-identically. The pinned property is about the implementation rather than the corpus - the AS frontend has zero to_uppercase sites and its three lowercasing sites are all value-level - which is what makes it pinnable at all. THE DEFECT FOUND: subst_frame_text replaced one name at a time over the whole line, so `mm qq,zz` on params pp,qq emitted E<zz,zz> against asl's E<qq,zz>, and `mm xx,pp,yy` gave E<xx,xx,yy> against E<xx,pp,yy>. New substitute_frame in expand.rs walks the line once in AS's precedence and never rescans what it appends. VERIFIED, re-checked here rather than accepted: strict landing run at the exact final tip 5e8cf46a, branch clean, 376 suites 4277 passed / 0 failed / 2 ignored, zero skip: and zero ratchet:, CARGO_EXIT 0, log stamped and carrying both new test names; baseline DERIVED by the agent from a worktree run at d37c1738 giving 4273 plus exactly 4 added #[test] items, which reconciles against my own independent 4273 measurement earlier today; clippy --release --workspace --all-targets -D warnings re-run BY ME at exit 0 (the only claim with no artifact left behind); all four aeon shapes deleted and rebuilt at 16:10-16:16Z from the 620f8b7d binary under SIGIL_VERSION_STRICT=1, CRC32+size matching the frozen tip on every one, mtimes confirming the rebuild; corpus diagnostics hold at 22,328 with sorted sets identical by diff. Byte-neutrality deliberately NOT re-run at 5e8cf46a, and I verified that shortcut rather than granting it: every changed .rs line in that commit is a /// doc comment, checked by filtering the diff. Pre-merge bar by derivation: merged tree hash equals branch tree hash. NOTABLE, and the agent's own honesty is the reason it counts: one of its mutations left a test GREEN, and rather than accept it as a pass it chased down why (surplus positional arguments bypass bind_macro_arg) and replaced it with one that covers the path - invariant 8(c) working as intended. FOUR PLACES MY BRIEF WAS WRONG, all corrected by its evidence: the case divergence was a probe artifact; lib.rs's 'case-sensitive' line is at 148 and scoped to -D defines rather than being a namespace-wide declaration; aeon's %<...> debugger strings interpolate parameters and not ALLARGS, and aeon has zero shift uses; s2.asm carries two shift statements, not one. STILL OPEN: positional-after-keyword, where the gap underneath is that sigil raises no #1812 refusal at all, so matching asl means implementing the refusal rather than the rendering. Booked: a plain label in a macro body does not export in asl (only `nm label *` does) while sigil resolves the plain form and has no label directive; and surplus positional args skip caller-scope dot-local qualification.

headline: The rule that stopped one macro seeing a value another set for it is fixed, and the real assembler turned out to answer the hard case differently depending on how many passes it happened to make.
matters: Two things worth your time here. First, we had the right conclusion for the wrong reason: our records said the assembler treats labels one way and variables another, and it does not - it goes by how the name is WRITTEN. A name written as a plain label with a colon belongs to the macro; a name written with any of the assignment spellings belongs to whoever called the macro. That distinction matters because one of the assignment spellings produces an address, so 'labels versus variables' would have got it backwards for that case. Second, and this is the part I want on record: the dangerous case the row was sized around - a macro's own jump silently landing on a same-named label in the caller - is not a hazard we might accidentally introduce. It is what the real assembler DOES, and it does it inconsistently: the identical source gives one address in a simple file and a different address once something unrelated forces the assembler to make a second pass. We deliberately did not copy that. We work out which names belong to the macro once, before the body runs, so there is no lookup order for a pass count to perturb, and the situation cannot arise. The price is one case we refuse where the assembler quietly accepts: a label declared inside an arm that was not taken. I ratified that trade rather than letting it land as an implementation detail, because a reasonable person could argue we should bug-for-bug match instead - and my reason is that a compatibility surface should reproduce its original's SHAPES, and an address that depends on the pass count is not a shape.
detail: Landed at master 9aaba5a8 (merge of parcel/as-maclocal-scope, 8 commits 4efc5a0a..e3bc1618, one source file plus its note), pushed and verified by ls-remote. THE ESTABLISHED RULE, each half with a quoted asl -L row under the corpus's own flags including -U: a plain `.name:` colon label is expansion-scoped and never enters the symbol table (a reference from outside gives asl error #1010); `.name equ` / `=` / `set` / `:=` / `label *` all write the CALLER's scope and list as Base.name, so `label *` yields an address and is still caller-scoped - which is why the labels-vs-variables framing was wrong. Nesting is transparent to a binding; shift does not interact, since the scope is answered by the name rather than by frame state. THE DESIGN: the expansion-scoped set is computed from the body once by scan_dot_labels before the body runs, so there is NO lookup order and therefore no pass and no reference position can change the answer - the fall-through state does not exist rather than being avoided. asl reaches it non-confluently (67FE in a one-pass file, 6704 once an unrelated forward reference forces a second pass). VERIFIED BY ME ON THE MERGED TREE, not accepted: this agent left no suite log on disk, unlike the previous two, so I merged locally without pushing and ran scripts/landing-run.sh myself against .aeon-as-fold - 376 suites, 4290 passed / 0 failed / 2 ignored, RESULT GREEN, CARGO_EXIT 0, zero skip: and zero ratchet:, with all 13 new tests present by name in my own run's output; 4290 - 4277 = 13 = the added #[test] count, reconciling against the 4277 I measured independently at the previous landing. clippy --release --workspace --all-targets -D warnings re-run by me at exit 0. Merged tree hash equals branch tree hash. aeon: all four artifacts deleted and rebuilt at 17:28-17:33Z under SIGIL_VERSION_STRICT=1, CRC32+size matching the frozen tip on all four, mtimes confirming; the two commits after the byte proof touch zero non-docs files, which I verified by filtering rather than granting. I also confirmed target/release/sigil in the shared checkout still carries its 2026-09-02 mtime, so neither of my two cargo invocations relinked the assembler another lane may be mid-freeze with. CORPUS: 22,328 -> 21,003, a fall of 1,325 against my predicted ~1,300. Both target classes go to ZERO (org needs a constant expression 669 -> 0; brace-in-symbol-name 646 -> 0); 73 classes unchanged to the count, zero new classes, zero classes rose; sorted unresolved-symbol sets show zero newly unresolved and five newly resolved. s2.macros.asm:191 1,224 -> 0, :208 68 -> 0, :227 23 -> 0. TWO METHOD FINDINGS WORTH MORE THAN THE PARCEL: (1) the fall-back-chain alternative was GREEN against the agent's first nine tests, because sigil's environment survives a pass and a fall-back reaches the same answer - it treated that as runner blindness rather than a pass and built the untaken-arm gate specifically to discriminate, which now reds that mutation and nothing else. Second consecutive agent to self-catch a vacuous gate. (2) its own first cut required the label at column 0, which is exec_one's rule for a BARE head and not a colon one; aeon's diag_assert_vector rows caught it because aeon writes an indented `.skip:`, and the frontend's own tests structurally could not, since every one of them wrote the label at column 0. A test suite that shares a blind spot with the code it tests is invisible from inside. STAYS OPEN, all three in the note: an expansion-scoped name pasted into text via ALLARGS carries the deliberately-unspellable scope name and now REFUSES loudly where it previously panicked (closing it properly needs an identifier-legal reserved prefix, trading impossibility of collision for improbability); a plain global label inside a macro body changes the caller's dot-scope, confirmed real and left alone as the same territory as the label-export row; and {INTLABEL} / __LABEL__ / the label directive stay unimplemented, now the largest single block in s2.macros.asm at 492 diagnostics.

headline: Complaints fell another 5,381 to 15,622 - but the part that matters is the half of this defect that produced no complaints at all, and quietly bound every zone's constant to the wrong kind of value.
matters: This is the one I would most want you to read, because it is about the number I have been reporting to you all day. The row was booked at 492 complaints and delivered 5,381, and the consequential part of it was invisible to that count entirely: one macro was binding every zone constant to a position in the file rather than to its value, with ZERO complaints, and seven more sites were broken in a way that only shows up at the final linking step, which the measurement never reaches. So a complaint count tells you what the assembler REFUSED, and the faults this project keeps finding are the ones where it refused nothing and produced something wrong. Five of those closed today, and the two biggest were invisible to every measurement we had. I have written that into the lane's standing rules: a falling count is evidence that noise went away, never that correctness improved, and sizing work off it systematically under-prices the dangerous parcels and over-prices the loud ones. The things that DO see this class are the per-class breakdown, comparing the sets of unresolvable names in BOTH directions, byte-identity against the game, and simply reaching the link step at all.
detail: Landed at master c6c6bf49 (merge of parcel/as-intlabel, 8 commits b84e2c6a..a90eb104, two source files plus its note), pushed and verified by ls-remote. SEMANTICS, each with a quoted asl -L row under the corpus flags incl. -U: {INTLABEL} SUPPRESSES the invocation's label definition rather than duplicating it (the label is absent from asl's symbol table; the same macro without the group lists it), consumes no argument position at any position in the list, and may be declared twice; __LABEL__ is a TEXT SUBSTITUTION not a binding - a fourth candidate beside .ATTRIBUTE/ALLARGS/parameters, bound implicitly from the label field, empty when the invocation carries no label, which is what makes the corpus's `if "__LABEL__"<>""` guard work and the bare `label *` on the false arm inert; `label` takes ANY expression (A label *, B label $2000, C: label *+4 -> 1000/2000/1004), carries the segment, exports out of the expansion, and OPENS the caller's scope, which outlives it. THE RESHAPING FINDING: all four substituted names share ONE boundary rule - reject where an alphanumeric abuts an edge that could continue an identifier; `_` is an identifier char but not alphanumeric so it never blocks, and .ATTRIBUTE differs only through the per-edge test since a leading `.` cannot continue an identifier. sigil had three different wrong answers. That rule is a STANDALONE DEFECT, not an enabler for the capture: zoneID macro zoneID,{INTLABEL} bound every zone constant to a PC with zero diagnostics, and seven ordinary-parameter sites (palptr macro ptr -> ptr_End-ptr, 41 invocations) failed only at LINK. VERIFIED: two stamped suite logs left on disk as I required after the previous agent left none - /home/volence/probe-intlabel/landing-branch.log (376 suites, 4302 passed / 0 failed / 2 ignored, exit 0, zero skip:/ratchet:) and landing-master.log at 6446259c (4290/0/2), difference 12 = added #[test] count; the master baseline REPRODUCES EXACTLY the 4290 I measured independently on the merged tree at the previous landing, which is what makes the pair worth something. Suite and byte proof both at 788648db; the tip commit a90eb104 touches 0 non-docs files, verified here by filtering rather than granted. clippy --release --workspace --all-targets -D warnings re-run BY ME at exit 0; target/release/sigil still at its 2026-09-02 mtime, so my verification relinked nothing. aeon: all four deleted and rebuilt 18:30-18:35Z one shape per invocation under SIGIL_VERSION_STRICT=1, CRC32+size identical on all four. CORPUS 21,003 -> 15,622 (-5,381), EVERY diagnostic line classified with no unclassified remainder, no class rose, no new class, 135 of 163 classes unchanged to the count, and the sorted unresolved-symbol sets show zero newly unresolved AND zero newly resolved. THE APPLIED-AND-GREEN, third consecutive agent to self-catch one: dropping builder.define_label stayed green across the whole crate because the frontend folds the symbol from its own env on the converged pass, so a label binding an equal-valued CONSTANT produces identical bytes even through a bra.w the linker fills; the gate now asserts at the IR against the plain-label twin and reds. FIVE PLACES MY BRIEF WAS WRONG: five corpus files not four (mappings/MapMacros.asm is the fifth and is 85% of the whole fall - my grep globbed only the top level and missed the subdirectory); the block is 5,381 not 492 (492 is exactly right for s2.macros.asm:157, which is 9% of it); 21,003 was NOT stale and reproduced exactly; `label` is not 'defines it at the current address' but takes any expression and opens a scope, and that scope-opening nearly broke zoneOrderedTable because the scope had been arriving from the very definition {INTLABEL} suppresses; and the block has the silent half above. Its own process note is worth keeping: a doc-only commit moved HEAD mid-build-chain and the strict revision gate correctly refused two shapes, so it relinked and rebuilt all four from one binary rather than reasoning forward - the version-provenance gate doing exactly its job. OPEN: irpc (s2.macros.asm:289, 272) and the three largest remaining sites, all in s2.macrosetup.asm (996 + 749 + 749), none of them this row; the booked plain-label export row is unmoved and was verified byte-identical before/after rather than traded against; a non-PC `label` binds and opens scope but claims no position, unreachable today; two interactions probed and recorded but not separately gated because no mutation reds them that the capture tests do not already.

headline: Three names the assembler never defined were silently choosing the wrong processor's code path, so the Z80 versions of five basic directives were what ran when assembling 68000 code - no error, correct exit code, wrong bytes.
matters: This is the worst thing found today and it is the clearest example yet of why the complaint count cannot be trusted as a health measure. Three names the setup file tests - one holding which processor we are building for, and the words for true and false - were simply not defined by us. An undefined name reads as false, so every test of the form 'if this is not a Z80' came out false, and the Z80 versions of five fundamental directives (setting the address, aligning, padding, reserving space) were what assembled while building 68000 code. On a one-file test the real assembler emits 11 33 and we emitted 22 44 - with a success exit code and not one complaint. And it could never have shown up in the number I have been reporting you all day: a name consumed by an IF never reaches an operand, so our own run mentioned these three names exactly zero times. What found it was following the advice I put in the brief - go all the way to the LINK step, which a complaint run never reaches. A four-line probe that assembles AND links says 'unresolved symbol' immediately. The two loud faults underneath were real too: one line failing to tokenise made us lose track of which conditional block we were in, and our own function-argument substitution was wrapping arguments in parentheses that then broke the string builtins.
detail: Landed at master 89f0bffb (merge of parcel/as-macrosetup-sites, 3 commits c23d3216/9bb1c9ad/7f9b0006, eval.rs + lexer.rs + note), pushed and verified by ls-remote. DIAGNOSIS WAS THE DELIVERABLE AND IT CAME BACK TWO CAUSES, NOT THREE: the 996/749/749 split is real but sits at s2.macrosetup.asm:104, :59, :62 - none of the macros my brief named. :59 and :62 are ONE cause and the equal counts were the tell: dispatch_head lexed with lex_line(...).ok()?, so a line whose OPERAND failed to tokenise had no head at all and block-structure scanning lost it - the `if ($)&1` at :59 vanished, :61's endif closed the OUTER conditional, and :62's endif had nothing left to close; asl counts nesting inside a branch it never evaluates. :104 is separate and not about strlen: expand_calls substituted every user-function argument PARENTHESISED, so chkop's own strlen(ref) was handed ("0("); asl folds all eight paren-wrapped forms and master failed all eight. THE SILENT HALF: MOMCPU, TRUE, FALSE undefined (asl: dc.l MOMCPU => 0006 8000, dc.b TRUE,FALSE => 0100), so `if notZ80(MOMCPU)` and `if TRUE` read FALSE and the Z80 arm of org/cnop/align/even/ds assembled under the 68000. Byte witness on one file: asl 11 33, master 22 44 exit 0 zero diagnostics, branch 11 33. HOW IT WAS FOUND, which is the reusable part and is exactly the discriminator I put in the brief: the master corpus run names MOMCPU zero times and TRUE/FALSE zero times, because a name consumed by an `if` never reaches an operand - so the metric was structurally blind, again. Reaching LINK surfaced it in four lines (`unresolved symbol MOMCPU for fixup`), which is why the new gates use linked_image rather than image. It ALSO probed the byte-silent shape of the loud cause and it did NOT reproduce (find_block_end's stack of closer sets absorbs it; a desync always consumes a closer and always leaves one unmatched), so cause A is loud at the wrong line, never silent - a negative result stated rather than assumed. CORPUS 15,622 -> 13,830 with the per-class decomposition summing to the totals both times: strlen 996->0, `$ with no hex digits` 752->0, macrosetup mnemonic 751->2; sets compared both directions, zero newly unresolved, two newly RESOLVED (d0, d4). FIVE CLASSES ROSE and each was checked individually and accounted for as ground the frontend now reaches rather than regression - with org working it gets further. That is the right handling of my own banked rule: the rule asks whether a class rose, it does not forbid it, and an accounted-for rise is a different object from an unexplained one. VERIFIED HERE: suite log at .sigil-macrosetup/.target-land/landing-macrosetup.log stamped pwd/HEAD 9bb1c9ad/branch clean - 376 suites 4310 passed / 0 failed / 2 ignored, zero skip: and zero ratchet:, exit 0, reconciling the 4302 master baseline + 8; all EIGHT new test names extracted from the diff and each confirmed present exactly once in that log by me rather than taken from the report; tip commit 7f9b0006 touches 0 non-docs files, filtered here; red-first log shows the correct shape green(8) -> RED 3 -> RED 2 -> RED 3 -> green(8); clippy re-run BY ME at exit 0; aeon all four deleted and rebuilt 19:13-19:18Z byte-identical to the frozen tip; target/release/sigil still at its 2026-09-02 mtime. BOOKED WITH MEASURED SIZES: AS-MACRO-BANG-SHADOW 626 (the corpus's new largest site - `!ds.ATTRIBUTE` recursing into the shadowing ds macro), AS-MACRO-ARGCOUNT-IRP 272, AS-INSN2OP-DISP-OPERAND 162, AS-WARNING-EXITM 60, AS-ATTRIBUTE-BANG-ADDI 40, AS-WORD-IMM-RAM-LABEL 34, AS-CNOP-ORG-CONST 1. MY BRIEF WAS WRONG ABOUT THE SITES ENTIRELY - none of the macros I named carries any of the three - and the prior note's hypothesis (ARGCOUNT, irp, the Z80 $ program counter) did NOT survive: ARGCOUNT/irp are not in the top three and $-as-Z80-PC always worked; :59's $ error was CORRECT 68000 behaviour reported from a line that should never have been reached. ITS OWN DISCLOSED GAP, accepted rather than papered over: lex_line_recover_keeps_the_head_before_a_bad_operand has no mutation gate, because removing the function fails to COMPILE rather than failing red - an honest statement that one of the eight is pinned by construction rather than by a proof.

headline: Sent an agent at the biggest remaining pile of complaints; the pile was real, but underneath it two of the most basic directives in the disassembly had been running from the wrong table all along, silently.
matters: The disassembly defines its own versions of some builtin directives, and uses a prefix to say 'I mean the real one, not mine'. We had both halves wrong: we checked the builtin table before the macro table, so a macro that shadows a builtin never ran at all, and the escape prefix was being stripped and re-looked-up, so it walked straight back into the macro it was escaping. The complaint pile was one site, 626 of them. The part with no complaints was bigger: setting the address and aligning are the only two of the disassembly's 187 macro names that collide with our 25 keywords, so those two ran from the wrong table across the entire corpus and said nothing. That is the third time today the quiet half was worse than the loud half, and the agent found it with a byte probe rather than by reading code. Two other things came out of it worth knowing: a fix for a separate silent fault - reserving space left the write cursor alone, so output came out twenty bytes short with no complaint - is written and proven but deliberately parked, because landing it needs a question settled first. And that question is now the thing I have running, because it decides real addresses in the shipping game and our own byte checks cannot answer it.
detail: Landed at master 26600e3f (merge of parcel/as-bang-builtin, 2 commits 74f19b78 + note 768383fa, eval.rs + note), pushed and verified by ls-remote. THE RULE, six asl probes each quoted: a user macro beats the builtin of that name, DIRECTIVE AND MNEMONIC alike (with org and move macros in scope, `org $200` runs the macro and only `!org $300` seeks); `!name` resolves in the builtin table and NOWHERE else - it is not a fallback, `!mym` on a macro-only name is `#1200 unknown instruction`; the `!` is glued to the name, `! ds.b 3` with a space is an empty mnemonic; it composes with a colon label; .ATTRIBUTE carries the invocation's suffix and ALLARGS its args through the escape. TWO MECHANISMS ONE RULE: dispatch matched the keyword table before the macro table, and `!` was stripped and re-dispatched into the macro it escaped. THE SILENT HALF, larger than the row: org and align are the only 2 of the corpus's 187 macro names colliding with its 25 keywords, so both ran from the wrong table corpus-wide with zero diagnostics; found by a byte probe reaching link, not by reading code. THE TWO ROWS DO NOT SHARE A CAUSE, contrary to my brief: AS-ATTRIBUTE-BANG-ADDI's 40 are all unresolved-symbol, the line already reached builtin addi/subi, and all 16 distinct names trace to an objoff_XX from three enum lines at s2.constants.asm:133-135 - re-booked as AS-ENUM-DIRECTIVE (40+31) because the old name named the wrong cause. SILENT-HUNT METHOD, stated because the method is the reusable part: byte probe reaching link on the shadowed shape; precedence probe which found the large half; all 695 corpus `ds` sites enumerated and classified (639 in a phased RAM block, 56 in two STRUCTs, all address-only); aeon's three .asm files contain zero `ds`, the grep being the fact. VERIFIED HERE: suite log at .sigil-bang-ds-target/landing-bang-builtin.log stamped, 376 suites 4314 passed / 0 failed / 2 ignored, zero skip:/ratchet:, exit 0, reconciling master baseline 4310 + 4; tip 768383fa touches 0 non-docs files, filtered here; clippy re-run BY ME at exit 0; aeon four shapes deleted and rebuilt 20:39-20:44Z byte-identical; assembler mtime still 2026-09-02. A PROOF-PROVENANCE CHECK WORTH RECORDING: the red-first log's baseline names tip 38284f73, which is on the PARKED branch and not the commit I landed. I diffed the two eval.rs blobs rather than accepting it: they differ by doc-comment whitespace plus one extra reserve-related test, so the proof tree was a SUPERSET of the landed tree, the mutated code and the four redded tests are identical in both, and the proof transfers. That is a check nothing in the report would have prompted, and the honest alternative was that a proof had been taken against different code. PARKED AND MUST NOT BE LOST: parcel/as-reserve-materialise at 68386152, three commits touching crates/sigil-link/src/lib.rs and relax.rs - an already-red-first-proven fix for a reservation leaving the write cursor alone (asl+p2bin `11 00 00 00 00 22` vs sigil `11 22 33 44`, twenty bytes short, exit 0, no diagnostic). It reddens five suite expectations encoding the packed model, one of which is the very align-in-phase test the next row is about. FLAGGED AND NOW RUNNING: three probes say `align` inside a `phase` is a plain round-up of the LOGICAL address ($B005 -> $B100, $B000 -> $B000), contradicting directive_align's recorded 2026-07-08 rule and the test at eval.rs:7729 asserting [0xB2,0x00]. It decides aeon RAM addresses - debugger.asm is in the shipping build path with 21 align occurrences - and it is the shared-frame class our gates cannot see: the goldens were produced by this implementation, so a wrong rule is carried identically by both sides of every byte check. Dispatched with asl as the only admissible oracle and an explicit instruction that a moved aeon byte is a BLOCKED report, never something to adjust the fix around.

headline: Sonic 1 stands at 9,739 errors - and 90% of them are two directives on sixty lines of source. It also comes with something Sonic 2 never had: the real retail cartridge to check ourselves against.
matters: Three things here, and the last is the one I would keep. First, the number is honest: 9,739, and it covers the WHOLE disassembly rather than stopping at the first problem, which the agent proved by planting a marker in each of the 444 files and checking both assemblers reported them - so you can read it as a real total rather than a floor. Second, it is far more tractable than the number suggests. One directive accounts for 8,211 of the errors across 59 lines, and a second accounts for 615 on a SINGLE line, because a macro invoked 615 times reports once per invocation. Two directives, sixty lines of source, ninety percent of the problem. That also means an error count is a bad way to size work, which is now the third separate demonstration of that today. Third and best: the Sonic 1 disassembly builds bit-perfect against the actual retail cartridge. Every check this project has used so far compares our output against reference bytes our own code produced - which is why a wrong rule can sit on both sides and they agree perfectly, exactly how the alignment defect hid. Sonic 1 hands us a judge from outside: a real ROM neither we nor the reference assembler made. That is a better reason to have switched than the one we switched for.
detail: Landed at master ecb69f5a (merge of parcel/s1-corpus-baseline, 4 commits, note plus evidence under .s1probe/), pushed and verified by ls-remote. Measurement only, zero .rs touched - verified by filtering the diff - so the suite cannot move and was not re-run. BASELINE: 9,739 diagnostics, all severity error, zero warnings/notes, running `sigil sonic.asm` from the corpus root against s1disasm f6ece657 in a detached worktree, sigil built fresh from master 5bd06567. Freshness witness, and it is the right kind: the same binary reproduces 13,109 on s2disasm, today's S2 figure hit independently, which I corroborated against my own lane log rather than taking. Bare-checkout caveat: gitignored generated DAC includes give 9,747; 9,739 is the corpus in the state the real build assembles. COVERAGE PROVED POSITIVELY, not by absence - a unique bogus head planted in each of the 444 files of the include closure, asl reporting 439, sigil 437, 436 shared. The three sigil misses are DPCM includes under CPU Z80 where it silently binds an unknown head as a label; the one sigil-only hit sits after END, which sigil does not honour. DECOMPOSITION sums with no remainder over 675 distinct sites: 8,939 unrecognized 68000 mnemonic (15 names) / 497 unresolved symbol (86 names, 496 struct members) / 161 operand out of range / 36 bad operand expression / a tail. RANKED: eval 8,211 on 59 lines (84.3%), irpc 615 on ONE line (Macros.asm:317, demoinput, invoked 615x), STRUCT+DOTS member addressing ~499, then 58 genuinely absent 68000 encodings (bchg 49, exg 4, roxl 2, move.w Dn,ccr 2, usp 1), macro default argument values 54. TWO SILENT CLASSES, found by probe not by count: under CPU Z80 an unrecognized bare head is SILENTLY BOUND AS A LABEL - no diagnostic, no bytes, exit 0 - so sound/z80.asm's six diagnostics are a floor and not a measurement, and an unimplemented Z80 mnemonic emits nothing while the ROM goes quietly short; and END is not honoured. Probed and confirmed CORRECT rather than silently absent: save/restore, phase/dephase, align, org, while, padding, supmode, string switch, shift, MOMCPU, ALLARGS. BYTE REFERENCE EXISTS AND IS RETAIL IDENTITY: the corpus's own lua build produces a ROM its chkbitperfect.lua calls bit-perfect with REV01, md5 09dadb5071eb35050067a32462e39c5f, crc32 afe05eee, 524288 bytes; asl assembles S1 with exit 0 and no log file at all. Three targets exist from one tree (REV00/REV01/REVXB); only REV01 was built. THE FINDING THAT REACHES OTHER WORK: the two asl binaries on this machine are DIFFERENT BUILDS behind one version string - S1 ships upstream (x86_64-unknown-linux, md5 61e672...), S2 the flamewing fork ((C) 2022-2024 flamewing, md5 0dee1f...), different sizes, both reporting AS V1.42 Beta Bld 212. I verified both firsthand. EVERY rule this lane established today was probed against the fork, and our July alignment note names no binary - so I relayed it to the align agent mid-flight as a better suspect than flags for that contradiction, with instructions to run both and to treat a disagreement as a BLOCKED decision about which build is the oracle, not its call. RE-RANKING INPUTS THAT INVERT THE OLD ORDER: eval was sized S against S2 at 3,417 and is now the project's front row at 8,211; S2's largest known gap, the 2,307 nameless +/- labels of d-22, is ZERO in S1; and `shift`, the parcel recovered this morning, has ZERO uses in S1 - correct and needed for S2, but the S1 ranking would not have chosen it. What S1 uses that S2 does not: dcb.b (20 sites vs 0), equ 1,104 vs 40, a 444-file include closure against S2's flat layout, the corpus's own RAM self-checks, float literals in irp, move.w Dn,ccr, and a Z80 sub-assembly that really switches CPU where S2 stays on 68000 via cpu z80undoc - which is the one that hides defects rather than reporting them. The agent also caught its OWN hypothesis with the oracle, declining to book a substitution bug after asl produced the identical error, and noted dcb.b is a corpus macro rather than an AS builtin. Peer-tree hygiene: its s1disasm worktree is removed, the registry is back to the main tree alone, and that tree's own four dirty entries are exactly as found - verified here, and aurora should still be told the registry was touched.

headline: The alignment rule we thought was wrong turned out to have been measured correctly two months ago - what got lost was that the addresses were negative, and that one dropped word made the rule wrong everywhere else.
matters: I reported this to you earlier as a straightforward mistake on our part, and that was my error, so here is what actually happened. In July someone probed the real assembler's alignment behaviour against the game's RAM addresses and wrote down four correct results. RAM addresses on this machine are negative numbers. The note recorded the four answers and not the fact that they were negative - and the test written from it used a positive address instead, where the assembler genuinely does something different. So the measurement was sound and a CONDITION was dropped between measuring and writing down. That distinction matters more than it sounds: a wrong measurement is caught by re-measuring, but a correct measurement with a missing condition looks exactly like solid ground afterwards, and it stood for two months. The real rule is that alignment is computed on the address read as a signed number, so RAM addresses round the opposite way and usually land a block high. Our game's addresses are unaffected - all four ROMs are byte-for-byte identical, and not by luck: the engine's assembly files use no relocated blocks at all, and its one aligned RAM symbol sits at a value where the old and new rules agree. Thirty-one measured rows are now committed with the exact assembler binary that produced each one, and a check that reproduces all of them.
detail: Landed at master cb4521d9 (merge of parcel/as-align-in-phase, 9 commits off 5bd06567), plus a prose fix to the frozen record's PROVENANCE.md which carried the same disproved sentence (no golden byte, no CRC, no pin). Pushed and verified by ls-remote. THE RULE: asl's `align n` computes the target on the low 32 bits of the PC read as a SIGNED i32 with C's truncating remainder, then advances by the unsigned difference - t32 = (int32)(pc+n-1); a32 = t32 - (t32 % n). Non-negative low half gets the plain round-up; negative rounds toward zero, so an already-aligned RAM address advances a full n. `phase` is irrelevant: org $FFFFB000 + align 256 gives $FFFFB100 with no phase present. Also recorded at the function and deliberately unmodelled: n truncates to a Word (align -256 acts as align $FF00) and align 0 aborts asl with SIGFPE. JULY WAS RIGHT, and I had told the hub twice it was not: all four July rows reproduce today under BOTH asl builds as RAM addresses; the test transcribed them to a positive phase $B000 where asl says $B100. The generalisation drawn from them, round_up(pos+n,n), disagrees with asl on 20 of 31 rows including 5 of the 11 RAM rows. The binary lead I sent mid-flight is CLOSED BY MEASUREMENT: the flamewing and upstream builds agree on all 16 discriminating rows, gen_org_both.sh reproduces it, and every row now names its binary and md5. AEON: byte-identical in all four shapes, zero differing bytes, each ROM deleted before its build - and the agent caught its own stale-artifact trap on the first attempt, where two sonic4 shapes exited 1 for want of SIGIL_EMIT and the untouched files compared equal, presenting as a clean pass. Byte-neutral for structural reasons: aeon's three .asm sources carry no phase at all, and the single @align(256) sits at RAM cursors $FFFFBA1A/$FFFFE350 whose low bytes are ones where old and new agree (for n=256 they part only at low byte $01). The overshoot is live and shipped - Player_Pos_Ring lands at $FFFFBC00 where a plain round-up says $FFFFBB00. VERIFIED HERE: suite 376 suites 4319 passed / 0 failed / 2 ignored, zero skip:/ratchet:, with RUNNER_EXIT=0 and an END_MARKER as POSITIVE completeness assertions - the run took 13 minutes and exceeded the ten-minute foreground cap, so it was detached and polled, which is the amended rule earning its keep on its first outing and a live counterexample to the 3m40s-4m03s I banked two hours ago (my note's own caveat, 'not guaranteed on a loaded machine', held). The five commits after the tested HEAD are docs-only, filtered here. clippy re-run BY ME at exit 0 because the agent did not report it. TESTS: the one legitimate red was rewritten rather than deleted, into three tests carrying their listing rows - the phased ROM address, the RAM address that really does overshoot, and the n=2 pair - and with the fix in and tests untouched it reddened alone, 233 passed / 1 failed. Its sibling align_outside_a_phase_is_a_standard_roundup was checked against asl FOR THE FIRST TIME and is correct; only its comment was wrong. New gate reproduces_every_measured_asl_row is red-first proven with two mutations shown applied from disk (plain round-up reds 14/31, the July rule reds 20/31). Two earlier suite runs were DISCARDED rather than adjudicated - one with AEON_DIR unset producing 371 refusals, one compiled across an edit. FOUR MORE BRIEF CORRECTIONS, all mine: 'debugger.asm with 21 align occurrences' was a substring grep counting _eh_align_offset and .__align_flag - there are 10 directives, all !align 2, all ROM, and a whitespace-delimited grep returns zero because every one is spelled !align; 'the fix is a byte-mover' was false; the Player_Pos_Ring block figures in the old comment describe a layout long gone; and 'flags are the first suspect' was refuted - identical flags, identical source, both binaries, and the variable was the address's sign. OPEN: .emp's own align (emit_align_pad, D2.29) still rounds up plainly, which is correct for every ROM section and is all aeon has, but a vars-side use would need the shared rule; parcel/as-reserve-materialise is untouched and now unblocked, its blocker reduced to three tests, and its five conflicts against master are the identical five plain master already has, so this parcel neither added nor removed any.

headline: Sonic 1 went from 9,739 errors to 1,367 tonight - one missing directive was 86% of it. And the fix quietly broke something that no error count could have caught, which the agent found and closed before it shipped.
matters: The headline is the drop: one directive, and Sonic 1 falls by a factor of seven. The reason it was worth so much is unglamorous - it is simply the processor-neutral name for an assignment we already had, and ours was locked to the 68000 because on a Z80 our spelling is a real instruction. Sonic 2 fell by 3,484 from the same fix. But the part I would actually keep is what happened underneath. The assignment has a form that only works when the name starts at the very first column; indented, the real assembler treats it as an instruction instead. Our first version had no such rule, and that meant an ordinary line like `dc.b eval&$FF` - which merely MENTIONS the word - was read as an assignment to a symbol named after the instruction, and emitted no bytes at all, with no complaint and a success exit code. The agent introduced that, hunted for it deliberately rather than trusting the falling number, found it, and the same guard turned out to close an identical hole that had been sitting in the older spelling all along. The count was 1,367 with the bug and 1,367 without it - it was completely invisible to the measure we were optimising. What found it was comparing actual BYTES: all 59 sound-voice banks in the game assembled and compared against the real assembler, 59 identical, and the same comparison against the previous build gives 59 differing, so the check can tell the difference.
detail: Landed at master b3f3d778 (merge of parcel/as-eval, 7 commits, rebased twice cleanly past the align parcel), pushed and verified by ls-remote. SEMANTICS, oracle s1disasm's own asl md5 61e672562465725a8c102288a7da9098 (upstream, NOT the flamewing fork S2 ships) with -U: eval is AS's processor-neutral spelling of SET over ONE symbol class - `a equ 1` then `a eval 2` raises the same #2030 that `a set 2` does. The design point is the gate: sigil gates the `set NAME,VALUE` arm to Cpu::M68000 so a Z80 `set 3,a` still lowers, and eval must carry NO such gate - asl assembles an indented `eval j,9` under CPU Z80 (=9H) while `set 3,a` on the next line is still CB DF. Corpus: 3 label-column + 68 operand-column, all in sound/_smps2asm_inc.asm. THE COLUMN RULE, which the row did not predict: colon-less `NAME eval VALUE` requires COLUMN 0 (indented, asl says #1200 unknown instruction and treats the name as the mnemonic; a colon peels at any indent). eval and set are ordinary symbol names to asl, so `dc.b eval&$FF` arrives as head dc.b with eval in body[1] - ungated it assigned a symbol named `dc.b` and emitted nothing: no bytes, no diagnostic, exit 0. Self-introduced, self-found, and the same guard closes the set twin that was wrong on master. NUMBERS, all post-rebase with master re-measured from a binary built at it: S1 9,739 -> 1,367, exactly two classes moving (unrecognized 68000 mnemonic 8,939->728 = the whole of eval; operand out of range 161->0, baseline cause 4 confirmed downstream), fifteen other classes unchanged to the count, 9739-8211-161=1367 with no remainder - arithmetic re-checked by me. S2 13,109 -> 9,625 by the same two classes (-3,417 -67), also exact. Unresolved-symbol NAME sets identical both directions, 86/86 and 291/291; sites 675->615 and 8,660->8,600 with ZERO sites appearing only in the after. So the row delivered 8,372 off S1 and 3,484 off S2 - 86.0% and 26.6%, both larger than the 84.3% it was booked at. THE SILENT-HALF HUNT, four ways and the method is the reusable part: every voice bank in the corpus assembled and byte-compared against asl per file - 59 files, 162 voices, 4,025 bytes, 59 identical and 0 differing, NON-VACUOUS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS because the same sweep with the pre-fix binary gives 0 identical and 59 differing; a third oracle in the disassembly's own commented bytes for GHZ Voice $00, reproduced by asl and sigil from nothing but eval accumulators; a 27-case matrix on exit code AND bytes, 25 matching with 3 pre-existing divergences booked; and the Z80 class next door, which is why the dispatch reach is widened to every CPU rather than moved from one gate to another. VERIFIED HERE: suite 377 suites 4,324 passed / 0 failed / 2 ignored, zero skip: and zero ratchet:, zero FAILED lines, CARGO_EXIT=0, reconciling the agent's own derived baseline of 4,319 + 5 new tests; log stamped at faa97a7e and the tip a55e6c10 is note-only, filtered here; clippy --all-targets re-run BY ME at exit 0; and I verified its self-provisioned reference tree rather than trusting it - .aeon-eval-ref sits at the exact provenance tip 4f5ad5a1 with all four shapes matching the tip's CRC32+size, so its byte gates ran against a valid reference. ONE APPLIED-AND-STILL-GREEN CHASED, fourth consecutive agent to do so: an arity test matched the bare substring `eval`, which a no-eval build's own 'eval is not a recognized 68000 mnemonic' message also contains - tightened to the directive's own text. Two mutations shown applied from disk and restored from committed baselines; 12 asl-generated golden blocks whose regeneration is a git-clean no-op, so every committed byte is asl's. OPEN, all pre-existing and proven so by running the pre-fix binary: `equ` then `set`/`eval` is not refused (needs constant-vs-variable symbol-class tracking); a column-0 bare label named `set` dispatches as the directive because set is in the Z80 mnemonic table, set-only, the eval twin works; three-operand eval refused rather than implemented, loud, zero corpus sites. Baseline note corrected: seeding only generated/*.inc reads 9,743 because those files BINCLUDE the .pcm/.dpcm beside them; with all four kinds seeded 9,739 reproduces exactly. Registry hygiene: it touched both disassembly worktree registries and removed both, s1disasm's live tree left in exactly its pre-existing dirty state; it did not touch .aeon-as-fold or the owner's aeon tree, provisioning its own instead.

headline: The twenty-byte-short fault is fixed - and the mutation that was supposed to prove it came back GREEN, which turned out to be the real find: a collision check that could not see the thing it was built to refuse.
matters: The fix itself is what it said on the tin: reserving space left the write cursor alone, so our output came out twenty bytes shorter than the real toolchain's, silently. That is now closed. The better story is the proof. To show a fix works you break it deliberately and check the tests notice. Three breakages were tried; two were caught immediately and the third was NOT - everything still passed. The agent treated that as a defect rather than a formality, and found real uncovered ground underneath: the code that reports how much space a section occupies was under-reporting it, and that number feeds the check that stops two things being placed on top of each other. So a section holding six bytes was being read as holding two, and something placed four bytes in looked like it collided with nothing - meaning the reserved space got quietly overwritten, THROUGH the very check that exists to prevent exactly that. Nothing in any error count would ever have shown it. That is the fifth time today an agent has hit a breakage that failed to break anything, and the fifth time chasing it found something real rather than a false alarm; I would treat that as settled practice now rather than a nice habit.
detail: Landed at master bf4bf3e3 (merge of parcel/as-reserve-materialise-landing, 6 commits), pushed and verified by ls-remote. Ninth parcel of the day. THE FIX: image_bytes' Reserve arm advances the write cursor and the image grows only where something writes - both halves of p2bin - so asl+p2bin's `11 00 00 00 00 22` is reproduced where sigil emitted `11 22 33 44`, twenty bytes short, exit 0, no diagnostic. THE THIRD MUTATION AND ITS FIND: reverting image_final_size's Reserve arm left the FULL WORKSPACE green, 4,326 passed / 0 failed. Chased rather than accepted: that function feeds the post-fixpoint overlap check and its Reserve arm had no gate anywhere. An understated extent does not corrupt the image directly - it misses a COLLISION. A section holding $11 / a 4-byte ds / $22 owns [lma, lma+6); read as [lma, lma+2), a pin at lma+4 intersects nothing and flatten clobbers the reserved range silently. The silent clobber arrives through the check built to refuse it. New gate a_reservation_inside_a_section_counts_toward_its_overlap_extent with a non-colliding control, proven red - under the mutation resolve_layout returns Ok - and the stale 'Reserve is a no-op' doc comments on image_final_size/overlap_diag corrected. SEVEN tests reddened, not the five the parked record claimed nor the three the align parcel predicted, because the align parcel added three ds-based tests after this branch was parked. All seven rewritten from p2bin output rather than from sigil, none deleted, and a new assert_p2bin_image helper pins size, tail and the zeroes between so the reservation's contribution is asserted rather than discarded. Ground truth from asl -xx -n -q -A -L -U -i . plus p2bin on four probes and three purpose-built shapes. CORPORA HOLD EXACTLY: S1 1,367 and S2 9,625 before and after, with the diagnostic streams BYTE-IDENTICAL by diff, so the decomposition and unresolved sets are identical by construction rather than by comparison. And it explained why they cannot move - both corpora exit in the front end before sigil_link::link is reached, the same blindness the short image exploited - and recorded that in the row so a future reader does not read the zero as 'no effect'. AEON: all four shapes deleted and rebuilt from the branch binary under SIGIL_VERSION_STRICT=1, CRC32+size identical on every one, re-verified by me after the merge; golden/, pins.rs, repin_pins.rs and repin.toml untouched. VERIFIED HERE: branch landing run 377 suites / 4,327 passed / 0 failed / 2 ignored, zero skip: and zero ratchet:, zero FAILED lines, CARGO_EXIT=0, reconciling the master baseline of 4,324 which the agent derived itself in its own worktree and which matches mine; the new gate confirmed present in its own run; the tip commit is docs-only, filtered here; clippy --all-targets re-run BY ME at exit 0. ITS OWN DISCLOSED CAVEAT, worth keeping because the honesty is the point: its first branch run came back with one red on version_reports_the_head_of_the_tree_it_was_built_from, because it committed the parcel note WHILE THE RUN WAS IN FLIGHT - the exact hazard this lane's boot doc documents. It said so rather than quietly re-running, and both logs are on disk. FIVE PLACES MY BRIEF WAS WRONG, and the first was the whole story: master had already landed the parked branch's first commit as 74f19b78 but only its eval.rs half, deliberately dropping the link-side stopgap, so rebasing all three commits would have replayed a duplicate - the fix was to rebase --onto from that commit and replay only two. The 'five comment-reflow hunks' were an artifact of that duplicate, and one of the five was not a reflow at all but a 57-line whole-test addition. Seven tests, not five or three. The blocker named in the record, align_inside_a_phase_advances_a_full_extra_block, no longer exists under that name - the align parcel had already rewritten it. And 'aeon byte-neutrality genuinely at risk' was wrong: aeon has no .asm reservation with image bytes after it in-section.

headline: Sonic 1 is down to 887 errors. The loop constructs landed - and hunting for what they might break silently turned up a bug in the OTHER game's code that makes every one of its jump-table entries wrong, with no message at all.
matters: The row itself did what it said: two loop constructs, 480 fewer errors in Sonic 1 and 308 in Sonic 2. What is worth your attention is the fourth thing found while checking the work did not break anything quietly. There is an operator written as a double tilde. The real assembler treats it as a logical NOT - it turns any non-zero value into 0 and zero into 1. We treat it as two bitwise NOTs, which cancel out and give the value back unchanged. Ninety-six places in the Sonic 2 disassembly use it, none in Sonic 1 and none in our engine, and it sits inside the macro that builds every jump-table entry in that game. So those entries have been computing the wrong thing, silently, and the way it surfaced was that a test harness emitted NOTHING AT ALL with a success exit code. It is booked rather than fixed, because changing an operator's meaning deserves its own parcel and its own sweep. Also worth knowing: the agent found one of these in its OWN first draft - it rendered a hex number as decimal, wrong bytes, no complaint, and the error count never moved. It caught that by comparing actual bytes against the real assembler, which is the third time today that method found something no count could.
detail: Landed at master 3d247e57 (merge of parcel/irpc-irp, 6 commits off e91f649f), plus 872cc6cf making a code doc comment precise. Pushed and verified by ls-remote. Tenth and eleventh landings of the day. SEMANTICS, oracle s1disasm's own asl md5 61e672562465725a8c102288a7da9098 with -U: irp walks the operand's top-level comma groups as RAW SOURCE TEXT, never evaluated ($FF stays $FF, 1+2 stays 1+2); irpc evaluates its operand as a string ONCE then walks the characters; both close on endm or endr; substitution is textual and case-sensitive under the macro-parameter boundary rule; a loop nested in a macro is substituted once at entry and replayed, so a shift in the body advances the frame without re-texting it. AN EMPTY LIST IS ONE EMPTY ITERATION, NOT NONE - which is why the corpus writes `if ARGCOUNT>0`, and what Sonic 1's commonest demo line rides on; a head with no comma at all is different (asl #1110, body skipped). THE OWED ARGCOUNT PROBE, ANSWERED: it is a SUBSTITUTION not a symbol - the listing shows its digits pasted into the body line - it folds case, obeys the boundary rule, substitutes inside strings, and YIELDS to a parameter declared with that name. Under shift it fits a THIRD rule, not either vector: before any shift it is the arguments written; from the first shift it is params minus shifts, which goes NEGATIVE; and it stops moving after max(params,args) shifts. Sixteen grid rows in the note. So the earlier parcel was right to refuse to state it, and the '3 -> 0' it had recorded is 1 minus 1. NUMBERS: S1 1,367 -> 887 (-480), S2 9,625 -> 9,317 (-308), decompositions summing with no remainder. The +152 and +75 RISES are the loops working - they land on bodies calling a float function sigil cannot fold, and both counts are derivable from source without the tool (8 calls x 12 items = 96; 12+12+12+12+12+10 = 70). Unresolved-symbol NAME sets 86/86 and 291/291, zero either direction; diagnostic SITE sets show 6 and 12 sites cleaned and ZERO new sites in either corpus. THE SILENT-HALF METHOD, which is the reusable part: all 13 Sonic 1 demo scripts wrapped in the corpus's own demoinput macro and compared against asl by CRC32+size across all 615 invocations - 13/13 identical - then PROVEN ABLE TO FAIL by dropping irpc's last character (13 differ) and by removing the boundary rule (13 differ), then restored (13 same). FOUR FINDINGS: (a) in its OWN first draft, irp items rendered from tokens printed $FF as 255 - wrong bytes, no diagnostic, count unchanged, caught only by the byte compare and fixed by slicing items out of the head text through token spans; (b) `~~` is asl's LOGICAL NOT while sigil computes double bitwise NOT - dc.b ~~0,~~1,~~5 gives asl 01 00 00 and sigil 00 01 05 - 96 sites in s2disasm, 0 in s1disasm, 0 in aeon, and it gates jmpTosInternal, i.e. EVERY S2 jmpTos; surfaced because a harness emitted nothing at all at exit 0; booked not fixed, since an operator change wants its own gate and sweep; (c) `NAME := <expr with an undefined symbol>` binds 0 silently where asl refuses with #1010; (d) a claimed correction to this morning's shift note which I CHECKED AND REJECTED - see below. A GREEN MUTATION CHASED AND DISCLOSED: making an empty irpc string yield zero iterations left all 13 harnesses identical, because demoinput's empty case falls to an empty else either way - so the empty-iteration rule is pinned by the probe and the test and by NOTHING in either corpus. Said plainly rather than left as a passing mutation. VERIFIED HERE: landing run 378 suites / 4,340 passed / 0 failed / 2 ignored, zero skip:/ratchet:, zero FAILED lines, CARGO_EXIT 0, reconciling the 4,329 baseline it derived itself which matches mine; log stamped and at the branch tip with no trailing commits; its 'DIRTY' stamp is untracked scratch only, confirmed here as zero tracked modifications; clippy --all-targets re-run BY ME at exit 0; aeon's four shapes byte-identical, re-measured by me after the merge. THE CORRECTION I MADE TO ITS REPORT, because taking it as written would have defamed correct work: it reported that a recorded, asl-verified project rule was WRONG - that the shift note read AS's placeholder bytes off a listing as nothing. I checked the note. It is right, and has a whole section titled 'Deliberately NOT replicated: AS's empty-parameter placeholder' with three listing-backed bullets stating exactly that a shift-vacated slot keeps the placeholder while a never-supplied one is genuinely empty. The measurement was sound; the characterisation was not. What was actually imprecise was the CODE's doc comment, which said 'empty fill' without naming the divergence - fixed at that size in 872cc6cf, pointing at the note's section. TWO SELF-REPORTED MISTAKES, both worth keeping: it deleted the reference tree's ROMs while a baseline run was reading them, invalidating that run, and killed and re-ran rather than reporting the number; and a master baseline run CONCURRENTLY with another returned 4,328/1 while the same suite alone is 4,329/0 - and it explicitly refused to let that be banked as 'a flake' from it, naming the falsifier instead (run the full suite twice concurrently on master). That refusal is the standard: an unestablished mechanism offered as an explanation is worth less than a named experiment.

headline: Sonic 1 is at 368 errors, and the disassembly's own three assertions about where its variables live now all pass - which is a better result than the number, because the game is checking us rather than us checking ourselves.
matters: The structure declarations landed: Sonic 1 from 887 to 368, Sonic 2 from 9,317 to 8,918. But the thing worth your attention is that the Sonic 1 source contains three assertions about its own memory layout - one of them says a particular variable must sit at one exact address or a routine misbehaves - and all three were failing before this and all three pass now. That is the game judging our work instead of us judging it by counting our own complaints, which is the second oracle from outside our own system that the switch to Sonic 1 handed us, after the retail cartridge. The other thing worth knowing is how the agent checked for silent damage, because a wrong structure moves every variable after it without saying a word: it dumped all 1,553 names in the whole memory map, assembled them with both tools, and compared the bytes - identical. Then it broke its own work six ways to check the comparison could notice; three of the six breakages produced NO failure at all, and rather than treat that as three passes it worked out why: those three rules are invisible to this particular game, so they are held up by the probes and the new tests alone and nothing in either disassembly would catch them going wrong. Saying that out loud is worth more than the three green ticks would have been.
detail: Landed at master db811a28 (merge of parcel/as-struct-dots, 6 commits off e45bc305; one non-docs file, crates/sigil-frontend-as/src/eval.rs), pushed and verified by ls-remote. Twelfth landing of the day. THE SEMANTICS, oracle s1disasm's own asl md5 61e672562465725a8c102288a7da9098 with -U, nineteen probes committed: asl keeps TWO offset tables per struct and they disagree - a ds.w at an odd running offset under padding on binds the DECLARATION symbol to the offset BEFORE its pad and the STRUCT ELEMENT to the offset AFTER, and an instantiation reads the element, so one declaration and one instance give two different answers for the same member (S.b=1 against inst.b-inst=2). An instance is never word-aligned; an embed is never re-aligned to the parent's parity, so an inner ds.w can land odd; DOTS is a property of the struct rather than of the instantiation site (a non-DOTS instance yields the underscore spelling and the dotted one is #1010); endstruct closes bare, name-in-label-column, or as ends. Three member shapes were unmodelled: markers (21 in one struct), embeds (18 flattened), and instantiation itself. NUMBERS: S1 887 -> 368 (-519: -496 unresolved symbol, -20 unresolved long expression, -2 mnemonic, -1 the corpus's own error), NO class rose, sites 609 -> 124 with zero new, unresolved NAMES 86 -> 1 with zero new and the survivor being usp. S2 9,317 -> 8,918 (-399), with +1 +1 on one new site which is the silent finding below. Both tables sum with no remainder. THE CORPUS'S OWN RAM ASSERTIONS: _Variables.asm 114, 430 and 486 all fired before; all three are gone after. 430 is the v_chunk0collision == ramaddr($FFFFFF00) guard, 486 the negative arm of the whole-map size check, so the RAM map now ends exactly where the disassembly says it must. The \{...} interpolation gap is unchanged so 430's by-how-much text still cannot be read - and it did not need to be, because the sweep gives the offset for every symbol rather than one. THE SILENT-HALF METHOD: a 1,553-symbol byte sweep of the entire RAM map, names read from _Variables.asm and the struct declarations and NEVER from an asl dump, dumped as dc.l and assembled by both tools - asl abc4c314/6212 == sigil abc4c314/6212, covering every RAM variable, every member of both structs, every embedded track's members, and the same layout again through the real instantiation. SIX MUTATIONS, three RED (markers dropped, DOTS ignored, ds.l width halved - each reddening by making line 430 fire again) and THREE GREEN, all three real uncovered ground rather than passes: instance alignment, embed re-alignment and the pre/post-pad split are invisible to this corpus because the instantiation lands even, the track length is an even $30, and neither struct has a wide member at an odd offset. Those three rules are pinned by the probes and the eight new tests alone, each red under its own mutation, and by nothing in either disassembly. A FOURTH GREEN CHASED: rounding the instance base left its own test passing because the label binds before instantiation runs - the row read the placement, never the base the members hang off; a probe now covers both. A SILENT ONE-BYTE STRUCT SIZE IN S2: 1upPlaying: ds.b 1 - asl accepts a leading-digit identifier, sigil's lexer refuses it, and the refusal was dropped by a bare .ok()?, so zVar.len came out $17 against asl's $18 with exit 0 on both sides, no diagnostic, and every member after it low. Fixed halfway ON PURPOSE: the lexer diagnostic is surfaced and an unread member line now says what it costs, while the leading-digit identifier rule is left as the identifier-surface question it is. A STALE-BINARY TRAP DISCLOSED: its mutation runner restored the source but not the binary, so a control stayed installed and produced a convincing false defect - the green sweep contradicted it, which is what exposed it; both runners now rebuild on restore and every affected ad-hoc measurement was re-run. VERIFIED HERE: branch landing run 378 suites / 4,348 passed / 0 failed / 2 ignored, zero skip:/ratchet:, zero FAILED lines, CARGO_EXIT 0, against a master baseline of 4,340 the agent derived SEQUENTIALLY rather than concurrently in its own detached worktree - 4,340 + 8 = 4,348 exact; the two trailing commits are docs-only, filtered here; clippy re-run BY ME at exit 0; aeon's four shapes byte-identical, expected since aeon writes zero AS struct lines, and re-measured by me anyway. FOUR BRIEF CORRECTIONS: my ~499-at-two-sites was low and S1-only (the real row was 477 S1 diagnostics plus 7 derived equates AND 315 in S2, which has four structs I never mentioned, one spelled in lowercase); there are exactly two declarations in total and the _Variables.asm site is the instantiation rather than a third; the oracle's message could not be read but there is a SECOND self-check I did not know about which also stopped firing; and the row was partly pre-existing, since the capture already had a padding model that turns out to match asl's declaration symbols exactly.

headline: An instruction the assembler did not recognise was quietly turned into a label, so the sound driver could come out short with no complaint - and the file that was supposed to be worst turned out to be clean, while the other game held the whole gap.
matters: This closes the last of the silent faults found this week and it is the clearest example of why a complaint count is the wrong instrument. Under the sound processor's path, an instruction we do not implement was being read as a label instead of refused - so it emitted nothing, the ROM came out short, and the exit code said success. Proof in bytes: three instructions where the real assembler emits four bytes and we emitted two, short by exactly the missing instruction. There was a second effect too, which bytes alone would not have found: the phantom label opened a naming scope, so every local label after it lost its home - three further complaints in Sonic 2 turned out to be collateral damage from instructions being swallowed above them. Now that unknown instructions are refused, the size of the gap is finally measurable, and it is small and specific: 22 instructions missing overall, but exactly ONE that either game actually uses, in Sonic 2's sound driver. Sonic 1 uses none - its sound vocabulary is fully covered. My brief was wrong about where the danger was: I sent the agent at Sonic 1's driver on the grounds that its six complaints were a floor, and for Sonic 1 the floor turned out to equal the measurement. The whole hidden gap was in the other game.
detail: Landed at master b590984f (merge of z80-unknown-head-loud) plus a follow-up merge for the provenance correction, pushed and verified by ls-remote. Thirteenth and fourteenth landings. THE SITE, and my brief named the wrong one: eval.rs:3216's arm chain already ends in an error, so anything reaching dispatch was loud. The silent bind is UPSTREAM at eval.rs:2011-2052, the bare-head branch of exec_line, where AS's column rule - column 0 is a label, indented is an instruction - was gated on `cpu == Cpu::M68000 || fold_kw(head) == "eval"`. Under Z80 nothing routed an unknown head to dispatch at all. Note the second half of that condition is the eval parcel's own column-0 guard from earlier the same night, so this parcel generalises a gate that parcel had made processor-conditional. The rule is processor-independent and the gate is removed. FOUR PROBE ROWS against S1's asl (md5 61e672562465725a8c102288a7da9098, -U): indented unknown head - asl #1200, sigil silent at exit 0, now names the head; column-0 unknown head - a label in both, unchanged; indented unknown head with operands - asl names the HEAD, sigil had named the first OPERAND, now names the head; indented `ldi`, a real instruction we lack - asl assembles it, sigil was silent, now refuses. BYTES: `nop / ldi / nop` at org 0 gives asl 00 ED A0 00 and gave sigil 00 00, exit 0. THE SECOND EFFECT: the phantom label opened a local-label scope, orphaning every dot-local after it - S2's .is_psg and .voiceptr, three unresolved-symbol diagnostics that were collateral damage and are repaired by the same fix. THE GAP AS A LIST: 22 Z80 mnemonics missing ISA-wide (cpd cpdr cpi cpir in ind indr ini inir ldd lddr ldi otdr otir out outd outi reti retn rld rrd sll), exactly ONE corpus-used - ldi, 17 sites, all s2.sounddriver.asm. S1 uses none. Seven implemented mnemonics are exercised by neither corpus. Cherry-picking ldi was explicitly rejected: the gap is now visible, which is what the row was for. CORPORA, and this is the set-vs-total rule paying off on live work hours after it was banked: S1 368 -> 368, TOTAL UNCHANGED AND CONTENT CHANGED, which only the set comparison shows; S2 8,918 -> 8,932 decomposing as +17 ldi now visible, +1/-1 a message change at one site at constant count, and -3 the repaired scope. A totals comparison would have reported +14 and missed all three mechanisms. BYTE SWEEP: 999 distinct corpus Z80 lines reduced to 255 self-contained, each assembled by both tools - 247 identical, ZERO differing, 6 sigil-refusals (ldi, sbc hl,bc, four ixl/iyl), 2 skipped. Proof of sensitivity: mutated an opcode in the Z80 backend, built the mutant to a SEPARATE target dir, got DIFFERS on that mnemonic and 247 -> 246; source restored from commit and the mutant binary destroyed. VERIFIED HERE: suite 378 suites / 4,351 passed / 0 failed / 2 ignored, zero skip:/ratchet:, zero FAILED lines, exit 0, reconciling the 4,348 baseline + its three tests; the trailing commit is docs-only; clippy re-run BY ME at exit 0; aeon's four shapes byte-identical, re-measured by me - and the new gate is LABELLED as unexercised by aeon, whose Z80 goes through the .emp front end rather than this path, which is the unexercised-gate rule from the previous parcel being applied unprompted. THE PROVENANCE CATCH, which is the reusable part: the report closed with 'corpus numbers re-run with the final binary (e8874800)', and e8874800 is not a valid object in this repo nor what the binary reports. I asked rather than banking it. It was the MD5 OF THE BINARY FILE, lifted from md5sum output and written in this repo's convention for naming commits - and a truncated md5 and a short SHA are the same shape, which is why it survived the agent's own review. The measurement reconciles exactly: the binary reports revision and closure-revision e20206f8, and `git log -1 HEAD -- <closure paths>` returns e20206f8, both checked here. The answer is stronger than the claim was - the landing-run binary and the corpus-measurement binary are byte-identical, two files in two target dirs from one clean tree, so a single program produced both the suite result and the corpus counts. The bad identifier never reached a committed artifact (zero occurrences on master and on the branch, checked). THE RULE: a provenance line that cannot be followed is WORSE than an absent one, because it consumes the reader's attention and returns nothing while reading as verified - and identifier-shape collision is how it survives review, since this project's artifact identity is a hash and its revision identity is a SHA and eight hex characters look identical either way. TWO MORE BRIEF CORRECTIONS: the hidden gap was entirely in S2, whose sound driver genuinely runs on the Z80 path under CPU Z80UNDOC - contradicting the S1 baseline note's claim that S2 reaches sigil still on the 68000, now corrected; and the retail-cartridge oracle is not reachable end-to-end because sigil reaches link on neither corpus, which the brief suspected and asked to have confirmed.

headline: An operator that cancelled itself out had been deleting 518 jump-table entries from Sonic 2 - not assembling them wrongly, leaving them out entirely. And the headline I gave you for it was wrong, which its own measurement proved.
matters: I told you this operator was picking the wrong instruction - choosing between two instructions of different lengths. That turns out not to happen, and the agent proved it rather than accepting my framing: the three tests are chained with an OR, every call site matches exactly one of the three, so the right answer and the wrong answer both come out the same and both emit the same instruction. Byte-identical with the bug present. I was confidently wrong about the mechanism from reading the source. What the operator was ACTUALLY doing is worse and simpler: it gated a block that builds jump-table entries, and with the gate inverted 518 of those entries were never assembled at all. Not mis-assembled - absent. That is why Sonic 2's error count went UP by 607 when this was fixed: the assembler can now see code it had been silently skipping past, and every one of the 607 reconciles to a specific block that was dark. Sonic 1 does not use the operator and moved by exactly zero, which was predicted in writing before the run and held so hard that the two error streams are byte-identical.
detail: Landed at master a9b1061b (merge of parcel/as-tilde-logical-not, 5 commits), pushed and verified by ls-remote. Fifteenth landing. THE OPERATOR: `~~` is ONE GREEDY TOKEN, asl's logical NOT; sigil lexed it as two `~` and folded the double complement, which cancels, returning the operand unchanged and silently. Listing rows: `dc.b ~~0,~~1,~~5,~~-1,~~$FF` is `01 00 00 00 00`; a single `~` is untouched (`FFFFFFFF FFFFFFFE FFFFFFF0`); `~~~` parses as `~~` then `~` by maximal munch; it binds at the ATOM tier, tighter than every binary operator (`~~0+1`=2, `~~0*3`=3, `-~~0`=FF); the only type rule is that a float operand refuses with asl #1134. Result type is an integer indistinguishable from a boolean, and asl's `||`/`&&`/`if` already take plain integers, so the operator is not a coercion the corpus needs - it is there for its meaning. BOTH SHIPPED asl BUILDS AGREE on every byte column and every error line including three refusals, so the fork/upstream control I asked for is clean and nothing here depends on which is asked. MY BRIEF'S HEADLINE WAS WRONG AND ITS OWN MEASUREMENT SAYS SO: I claimed the `_btst` macro selects `tst.b` against `btst`. The inversion is masked by the `||` chain - all 81 call sites pass an operand matching exactly one of three references, so `!A||!B||!C` and `A||B||C` both yield 1 and both emit `tst.b`. Measured byte-identical WITH the defect present (3dea1e5d/4136 both sides). I checked the arithmetic myself rather than take it: with exactly one of three true, both readings give 1; they diverge only when NONE match, which no call site does. THE REAL DAMAGE is `jmpTosInternal`, which deleted 518 jump-table entries rather than mis-assembling any. Also corrected: '96 sites' is 96 LINES / 99 occurrences (one line carries three). CORPORA: S2 8,932 -> 9,539, every one of the +607 reconciled - 518 ungated jump-table entries (515 plus 3 from a taken revision arm), 84 = 7 octaves x 12 notes behind an optimiser flag, 4+1 in two bug-fix blocks - all code sigil had NEVER assembled, so this is newly-VISIBLE ground rather than newly-broken. S1 zero movement with the two diagnostic streams BYTE-IDENTICAL at 368 lines each, backed by a coverage witness. PREDICTIONS WERE WRITTEN DOWN AND COMMITTED BEFORE THE RUNS (PREDICTIONS.md): S1 zero - held, harder than predicted; aeon byte-identical - held on all four; S2 rises - held, but the MECHANISM was half wrong and disclosed as such, since it predicted sets moving both ways and no line disappeared, those arms being diagnostic-free. A prediction that holds while its mechanism fails is worth more written down than remembered. BYTE SWEEP PROVEN ABLE TO FAIL: the jmpTos shapes DIFFER with the old binary - 36 bytes of jump table missing - and are SAME with the new; three other probes likewise DIFFER then SAME. THE GREEN MUTATION, CHASED: breaking the token renderer's arm left the suite green, because macro BODIES are stored as raw text and never reach the renderer - only macro ARGUMENTS do. A test was added for that path and LABELLED corpus-unexercised in its own doc comment, since no corpus writes the operator as a macro argument. VERIFIED HERE: branch 378 suites / 4,362 passed / 0 failed / 2 ignored against a master baseline of 4,351 the agent derived itself sequentially in its own worktree and which matches mine exactly, +11 being exactly the eleven tests added; both logs stamped, zero skip:/ratchet:/FAILED, exit 0; the two trailing commits are docs-only, filtered here; clippy re-run BY ME at exit 0; aeon's four shapes byte-identical, re-measured by me. BOOKED, not done: an unrecognised `even`; a trailing `align` at end of file emitting two bytes asl does not, which fails with BOTH binaries and so is ours; a string-returning function in a long address (the 518); the float frequency table (the 84); three asl refusals sigil accepts; and the empty-string operand never probed.

headline: Five instructions the backend never encoded are in - Sonic 1 is at 318 and has ZERO unresolvable names left. And the independent checker we brought in to be the trustworthy one turned out to be wrong about 64 instructions.
matters: Two things. First the milestone: Sonic 1's list of names the assembler cannot resolve is now EMPTY. It was 86 this morning, one an hour ago, and the last was a stack-pointer instruction we had simply never encoded. That is a floor cleared - you cannot emit a ROM for a game while instructions it uses do not exist. Second, and more interesting: this was the first row where we could check ourselves against something outside the project, an independent disassembler that learned the chip from neither us nor the reference assembler. It found nothing wrong with us - and we found something wrong with IT. It misreads a family of 64 instructions as a different instruction with the wrong operand size and the wrong source. The reference assembler refutes it and I verified those bytes myself before accepting the claim. That is the whole argument for having two independent checks rather than one: the one you brought in to be trustworthy is also a thing that can be wrong, and only the second one can tell you. The agent also found a test of OURS that asserted our own limitation as if it were a rule about the chip - the reference assembler assembles the thing our test said was impossible.
detail: Landed at master 916e398b (merge of isa-missing-encodings, 8 commits), pushed and verified by ls-remote. Sixteenth landing. INSTRUCTIONS: bchg, exg, roxl/roxr, move-to-ccr and move-to/from-usp, each implemented across its FULL addressing-mode matrix rather than the cells the corpus reaches, with the unexercised cells labelled - the entire dynamic bchg form, both exg pairs the corpus never writes, roxr altogether, nine of eleven ccr source modes, fifteen of sixteen usp words. There is no move-FROM-ccr on the 68000 and asl says so; the family is one direction. BOTH ORACLES COVERED EVERY INSTRUCTION - none single-oracle - and the two asl builds agreed on all 393 matrix probes. THE ORACLE WAS WRONG: Capstone decodes the 64-word cell roxr.b Dn,Dn as roxr.l #<ccc>,dN, wrong size AND wrong source, while reading the other eleven cells of that row correctly. asl refutes it twice and I VERIFIED BOTH ENCODINGS MYSELF rather than accept a claim that a third-party tool is defective: roxr.b d1,d5 = E235, roxl.l #8,d7 = E097, read off asl's own listing. New exclusion with its class size derived and asserted exactly rather than approximated. A SECOND FINDING OF THE SAME SHAPE AIMED AT US: the existing gate memory_shift_is_memory_only required asl.w d0 not to encode, asserting sigil's own limitation as a rule about the 68000 - asl assembles asl d0 to E3 40. Rewritten with byte witnesses. A THIRD, un-masked by the work: sigil never binds a label sharing its line with an `if` (Map_Ring: if Revision=0), standalone repro committed, gap-ledgered. A FOURTH, and it touches every freshness claim this project makes: the build banner NEARLY LIED - after an uncommitted edit to a file inside the binary's compile closure, `sigil --version` still said 'clean at capture', because cargo re-captures on HEAD movement only. The revision is a witness; the tree-state word is not. CORPORA: S1 368 -> 318 (-50) with THE UNRESOLVED-SYMBOL CLASS NOW ZERO, usp having been the last name; S2 9,539 -> 9,432 (-107). Both rises accounted rather than excused - S2's +10 is a class migration, 11 objoff operands surfacing behind former bchg heads minus the usp; S1's +8 is the label-on-if gap, feature-bisected and instrumented rather than inferred.
